Tiers (our descriptors, not canon terms): Unformed · Novice · Familiar · Practiced · Refined · Expert · Mastered · Transcendent. Store the tier in spells[i].proficiency and a 0–100 progress within the tier in spells[i].prog.
Improvement comes from real use and understanding. Combat and genuine need teach fastest; focused drills teach steadily; mindless repetition has diminishing returns. Tier-ups are notable events, typically weeks to months of use apart.
Mastery is more than damage: better efficiency (cheaper), casting speed, accuracy, stability, range and shape control, duration, output tolerance, casting while moving, multi-casting, resistance to interruption, and discovery of situational variants.
Variants: small structural changes (tighter, longer, split, delayed, dual) are recorded in spells[i].variants and do not create new pages. Fundamental restructuring can become a spell concept that may one day manifest a new page.
DETERMINISTIC GROWTH: An established spell's mechanics.manaUnits, mechanics.stamina, mechanics.fatigue and mechanics.impact remain stable through ordinary repeated casts. Spell proficiency and magic_profile.control/output modify the runtime cost/effect deterministically (formula in bc-spell-engine.js) — they do NOT require making up a new price each turn. A genuine structural breakthrough (greater size, changed form, a new sustained effect) may change the spell's base mechanics once, using [spells.<index>.mechanics: set {...}]. Preserve its identity and existing page; minor variants can have explicit profiles if meaningfully different. Never recalculate an old cost by random narration.

entries.name: Spell Shaping & Concept Development
entries.content:
SPELL SHAPING — Idea → experiment → failure → understanding → training → practical use → pressure → breakthrough → new page → mastery → variants.
A concept begins when the player describes an intent (the Shape form or plain text). Parse it into attribute + form + shape + behavior + range + power + speed + duration + precision + autonomy + special effect. Store or update ONE entry in spell_concepts: {"id","name" (working title),"intent","description","form","state","understanding","stability","control","experience","pressure","notes","updated"}. Numbers 0–100 are for you; the UI shows only Early / Developing / Stable / Refined / Resonant.
Compatibility first: IMPOSSIBLE (the attribute cannot produce it — Fire stopping time) or INCOMPREHENSIBLE (possible, but beyond current understanding). Show it through failed attempts, with one out-of-character line if needed.
Demands vs capability: output needed vs output; control needed vs control and spell control; mana cost vs reserves; complexity vs concentration and knowledge; similarity to things already mastered.
Attempt outcomes: Failed · Unstable (appears, then collapses) · Partial (some properties work) · Crude (repeatable but wasteful) · Functional (a reliable freeform technique, not yet a page) · Refined · Grimoire-Resonant (a candidate). Concept states: IDEA → EXPERIMENTAL → UNSTABLE → REPEATABLE → REFINED → GRIMOIRE_CANDIDATE → MANIFESTED.
Progress per attempt is small. Training blocks move understanding and stability over weeks. Combat use gives large experience at real risk. Watching another mage gives inspiration (a new concept of your own), never their spell. The same limit applies to being actively TAUGHT, not just watching: a trainer with a different
attribute can absolutely teach the FORM — what a good restraint actually needs (multiple
points of contact, redundancy against one break, immediate tightening), what a good Creation
needs, what a good Curse needs — as real, valid coaching (see training's trainer field). What
they teach is the functional principle, never a transferable spell; the student still develops
their OWN attribute's version through the normal concept pipeline, coached and accelerated, not
copied. A vine mage teaching restraint produces a vine-shaped lesson a fire mage can learn the
STRUCTURE from and nothing else — their own restraint will still be made of fire.
Oversized requests produce a smaller real thing first: 'a giant wind sword that cuts anything' starts as an unstable wind edge. Two mages with the same attribute and the same training still develop different spells, because concepts grow from each life's habits, imagery and needs (magic_profile.identity).
Existing spells can be shaped: smaller and faster, longer, cheaper, compressed, dual, released as a projectile, continuous, more penetrating. Small changes stay variants; fundamental restructuring may later manifest a new page.
Concepts can split (explosive burst, sustained reinforcement, midair redirection); each branch may remain a technique, become a variant, or eventually become its own page — decided by the magic's structure, not by RPG categories.
MECHANICS AT MANIFESTATION: When an actual new page appears, give spells[i] a mechanics object in the very same push directive: {"version":1,"tier":"small|standard|large|massive|utility","energyType":"mana","manaUnits":22,"stamina":2,"fatigue":1.5,"impact":19,"range":"variable","form":"Creation","duration":"instant"} (example, NOT universal). Derive the chosen tier and fields from the manifested effect, then persist them ONCE. The UI will normalize legacy spell objects with known deterministic defaults; do not create a second spell for this purpose. A spell's direct impact points are not inflicted HP until an actual attack connects and defense is established. Concept shaping can be evaluated freeform with a chosen tier and output, while the concept remains a concept and NOT an unwarranted grimoire page.

entries.name: New Page Manifestation & Breakthroughs
entries.content:
NEW PAGE MANIFESTATION
A new page can appear when enough of these converge: concept maturity (usually REFINED or GRIMOIRE_CANDIDATE), attribute compatibility, personal growth, practical need, emotional intensity, mana understanding, prior experimentation, grimoire resonance and breakthrough pressure.
Routes: TRAINING — months of development until the grimoire recognizes it (slow, calm); CRISIS — an extreme moment forces existing potential into a new expression (dramatic, never guaranteed); HYBRID — a trained concept completed by a crisis (the most reliable deliberate route). ORGANIC development also happens: repeated habits (say, always using fire defensively) become concepts the player never named.
Never: 'N days of training → spell', 'low health → power-up', or a page because the scene would look cool. If the conditions are not there, nothing happens.
When it happens, the grimoire reacts on its own — it opens, and a blank page fills with script. Generate the spell from what actually happened: attribute, concept, the moment, personality, imagery. Name it in canon style: '<Attribute> <Form> Magic: <Evocative Name>' (for example 'Wind Creation Magic: Gale Edge').
Write it immediately: [spells: push {"id":"sp-...","name":"...","attribute":"...","form":"...","page":N,"behavior":"...","range":"...","demand":"low|moderate|high|extreme","proficiency":"Novice","prog":0,"variants":[],"origin":{"date":"...","place":"...","trigger":"..."},"notes":"..."}], set the concept's state to MANIFESTED, [grimoire.pages_filled: +1], push to grimoire.history and to chronicle.
Pacing sanity: a young mage's first year might produce one to four pages depending on how intense their life is; growth later slows unless circumstances are extreme.

entries.name: Freeform Magic & Form Recognition
entries.content:
FREEFORM MAGIC — the player can attempt anything their attribute plausibly allows, without a spell page ('I compress the flame around my fist and release it on impact').
Evaluate: attribute, known spells, control, prior training, current reserves, similarity to what they have done, difficulty, stress and environment. Outcomes: failure · unstable partial success · temporary improvised technique · repeatable technique · variant of an existing spell · rarely, a new page under the manifestation rules. Freeform magic costs more and is less stable than a grimoire spell of similar scope.
Classify the form automatically from natural language: a limb wreathed in flame → Reinforcement; a flaming shield → Creation (defensive); binding someone → Restraining; a delayed trigger → Trap; lasting harm tied to a target → Curse; mending flesh → Healing; closing wounds or locking objects and magic → Sealing. The player never needs technical terms.
Casting: recorded spells are cast from the floating grimoire, which opens to their page; spell names spoken aloud are optional flavor. Casting time depends on familiarity; interruption depends on concentration and pain. Freeform is NOT capped at small and unstable just because a character has no grimoire yet, and a grimoire owner is never required to invoke the book for every act of magic either — canon shows Yuno using his own wind magic directly, unaided, even after he already has his grimoire. Evaluate freeform purely against the character's own control, output and training, in every era of their life: a high-potential or well-practiced mage is genuinely skillful acting on raw attribute alone; an average or untrained one is more likely small and rough. Talent and practice set the ceiling — not whether a book happens to be open.
FREEFORM COST BRIDGE: The player may use the story's Cast -> Freeform magic panel to describe the effect, choose utility/small/standard/large/massive SCOPE and restrained/normal/full output. The UI charges a deterministic higher cost than a same-scope recorded spell immediately; the GM still judges if the described result is possible and narrates failure, partial success or stable manifestation. Freeform casting from ordinary typed chat must use the same scale, proficiency and reserve rules: never invent another cost range. If no deterministic UI receipt exists, submit a structured freeform resource event or calculate with the documented formula; do not pretend a free-text cast was automatically charged. No grimoire or pre-existing page is needed to TRY freeform magic. Actual rare powers cannot be created by declaring their scope.

entries.name: Magic Attribute Registry — Canon
entries.content:
MAGIC ATTRIBUTE REGISTRY ([C] confident canon · [V] verify-level detail)
Families (engine categories): NATURAL (Fire, Water, Wind, Earth) · DERIVED NATURAL (Ice from Water, Smoke from Wind, Lightning, Plant, Sand, Stone...) · MATERIAL (Steel, Mercury, Cotton, Thread, Glass...) · BIOLOGICAL (Beast, Blood, Bone, Body) · SPATIAL · TEMPORAL · SOUL · IRREGULAR (Dark, Light, Shadow, Mirror, Dream, Sealing...) · CURSE-RELATED · SPECIAL.
Common attributes anyone may be born with: Fire, Water, Wind, Earth, Lightning, Plant, Ice, Sand, Smoke, Stone, Steel, and similar elemental or material domains.
Rare to very rare (allowed, socially notable): Spatial (Finral Roulacase, Langris Vaude, Valtos) [C]; Light (Patry) [C]; Dark (Yami Sukehiro — dark magic is slow, pulls in and absorbs other magic, and is Arcane-class against devils) [C]; Mirror (Gauche Adlai) [C]; Thread (Vanessa Enoteca) [C]; Transformation (Grey) [C]; Sealing (Secre Swallowtail) [C]; Shadow (Nacht Faust) [C]; Blood (Vanica Zogratis; the Witch Queen) [C].
Protected canon signatures — unique to their canon owners; never duplicated in Natural Simulation: Time (Julius Novachrono) [C]; World Tree (William Vangeance) [C]; Dream (Dorothy Unsworth) [C]; Briar (Charlotte Roselei) [C]; Mercury (Nozel Silva) [C]; Recombination (Henry Legolant) [C]; Soul (Lucius Zogratis, heavy spoiler) [C]; Star (Yuno, later reveal) [C]; Anti-Magic is not an attribute at all.
Other canon users worth knowing: Fire — Magna Swing, Fuegoleon, Leopold and Mereoleona Vermillion [C]; Water — Noelle Silva, Solid Silva, Lolopechka [C]; Wind — Yuno [C]; Lightning — Luck Voltia [C]; Plant — Mimosa Vermillion [C]; Steel — Klaus Lunettes [C]; Slash — Jack the Ripper [C]; Picture — Rill Boismortier [C]; Ash — Zora Ideale [C]; Cotton — Charmy Pappitson [C]; Ice — Heath Grice [C]; Beast — Vetto [C]; Mineral — Mars [C]; Smoke — Lotus Whomalt [V]; Earth — Sol Marron [V]; Body — Dante Zogratis [C]; Bone — Zenon Zogratis [C]; Gravity — the devil Lucifero [C]; Curse — the devil Megicula [C]; Word — the devil Zagred [V].
Attribute interactions are tendencies: Water has an edge over Fire; Lightning over Water; Dark absorbs; Mirror reflects — but output, quantity, construction, control, position and environment override tendencies.
Registry rules: canon spells stay with canon owners; sharing an attribute never means sharing a spell list; content from anime-only or film sources follows sim_settings.content_continuity.

entries.name: Random & Custom Attribute Generator
entries.content:
RANDOM & CUSTOM ATTRIBUTES
Random: choose a conceptual origin (natural phenomenon, material, organism, physical property, human-made concept, abstract phenomenon, unusual magical phenomenon) weighted by world rarity — most people get common natural or material attributes. Then generate domain, generation and manipulation rules, limitations, strengths, weaknesses, likely forms, rarity, mana behavior and visual identity.
Every generated or custom attribute passes five checks: CANON COLLISION (does a protected canon attribute already do this? 'Better Spatial' or 'Super Time' fail); SCOPE (absurdly broad concepts fail — 'Reality Magic: I change anything' is rejected; offer narrower readings such as Distortion, Probability-adjacent or Illusion); LORE (must obey Black Clover's magic laws); BALANCE (cannot quietly combine several exceptional canon powers); IDENTITY (must be genuinely distinct).
Generated magic gets real limits. Example — Glass: can generate glass and manipulate its own glass; possible blades, barriers, shards, mirrors, constructs; properties sharp, transparent, brittle, reflective; weaknesses impact fracture and brittleness; advanced potential refraction, layered armor, reflective defense, precision constructs. The attribute is a possibility space; the grimoire formalizes what the character actually learns to do.
Discovery: with Random, the character may only half-know their magic before the ceremony — childhood clues, family recognition, or genuine mystery — and the ceremony confirms it. Record the true attribute in magic_profile.attribute and whether the character knows it in magic_profile.attribute_known.
Full Sandbox may override restrictions deliberately; the world still reacts honestly to what the player has created.

entries.name: Magic Forms Registry
entries.content:
MAGIC FORMS — what magic DOES, independent of attribute
Creation: shapes the attribute into objects or creatures made of the caster's mana (weapons, constructs, animals). Barrier: pure defense, raised between the caster (or an ally) and harm; notably the one Form canon shows working as a raw, instinctive reflex, sometimes without a formal recorded spell at all — a strong barrier reaction under real threat is plausible even from someone who's never trained one deliberately [C]. Reinforcement: strengthens the body, weapons or objects. Healing: restores the body according to the healer's skill and the injury — it is not resurrection. Restraining: binds and holds. Trap: magic laid in advance with triggers (Zora Ideale's specialty) [C]. Curse: lasting effects tied to a target; curse-warding exists. Sealing: closes wounds, objects or magic (Secre's specialty) [C]. Transformation: changes shape or appearance. Recovery: restores stamina and physical exhaustion through special means — canon shows healing-adjacent magic relieving exhaustion this way [C]. Restoring another person's MANA specifically is rare and exceptional, not a normal effect: canon is explicit that even a dedicated exhaustion-relieving spell could not restore magical energy [C]; treat mana restoration as a genuine discovery or a rare, hard-won specialty, never a routine healing-adjacent service. Compound: two or more mages combining magic. Weakening: diminishing a target. Forbidden: methods using negative mana, sacrifice or devil contact.
Most mages specialize in one or two forms; wide versatility is a talent of its own. An attribute can support many forms, but a person develops only the ones their life trains.
Forms do not unlock like skills: a Fire mage who never practices healing does not suddenly heal. Unusual combinations (healing with fire, sealing with thread) are possible if the magic's properties support them and the mage develops them through shaping.

entries.name: Techniques — Reinforcement, Mana Sensing, Mana Skin
entries.content:
LEARNED TECHNIQUES (stored in techniques[], separate from grimoire spells)
Each technique record: {"id","name","category","source","teacher","tier","notes"}. Tiers use the proficiency words (Novice → Transcendent). Techniques are learned through instruction, observation plus practice, or hard-won self-discovery — never unlocked by points.
REINFORCEMENT: coating the body or an object with mana to strengthen it. Early mages do it crudely and expensively; skill makes it efficient and fast.
MANA SENSING: perceiving mana presence, rough size, attribute hints and spells gathering; range and resolution improve with training. It cannot read exact numbers, hidden intentions or unseen spell pages. Wind-attribute mages carry a latent natural edge toward this specifically — canon ties their affinity to a heightened feel for mana's flow [C] — so a Wind mage's sensing tends to develop faster and further than the same training would give someone else, without making sensing exclusive to Wind.
MANA SKIN: a maintained layer of mana around the body that protects against impacts and hostile environments. Requires sufficient control, output, sensing and stamina, plus real understanding. Progression: formation → stability → coverage → efficiency → strength → environmental resistance. It drains mana while active, and strong impacts, poor concentration, exhaustion or wild environmental mana can disrupt it; experienced users re-form it quickly. Mereoleona Vermillion is the canonical benchmark: she mastered it and Mana Zone through harsh mountain training in natural mana [C].
Teachers: a teacher cannot teach what they do not know. Teaching depends on skill, willingness, relationship, payment, faction rules and student capacity. A captain may refuse a stranger; a friend might teach for free; an institution may require membership.

entries.name: Mana Zone
entries.content:
MANA ZONE — controlling the mana of the surrounding area [C]
It is not extra MP and not '+25% damage'. The user extends awareness and control into ambient natural mana, which can let them draw on more power than their own reserves, perceive and react better, strengthen spells, and form attacks from unexpected points inside the controlled space.
Record: awareness radius, control radius, ambient mana available, control strength, precision, stability, spell integration, remote casting ability.
Requirements: high control and sensing, experience with natural mana, and real instruction or an intense natural-mana environment. It develops gradually through training in varied environments.
Environment matters: a mana-poor field gives little to work with; a Grand Magic Zone offers enormous mana but violent turbulence to control.
Contest: overlapping Mana Zones fight for control of the shared space; different parts of a battlefield can belong to different users.
Canon benchmark: Mereoleona Vermillion's overwhelming control of surrounding mana [C].

entries.name: Mana Method, Runes & True Magic
entries.content:
MANA METHOD — the Heart Kingdom's technique of forming rune arrays with natural mana to give instructions to magic [C]. Best suited to natural attributes but not strictly limited to them.
Runes are instructions the spell can actually perform — PURSUE, EXPAND, ACCELERATE, REPEAT, CONVERGE, ENCIRCLE, DETONATE, DELAY, DEFEND, RETURN — never 'WIN'. Arrays grow more complex with more instructions; complexity demands rune knowledge, natural-mana control, concentration and formation time. Unstable arrays fail or misfire.
It must be learned legitimately: travel to Heart, a qualified teacher, diplomatic access, or an alternate route the player builds. Canon default history: Clover knights train in Heart before Spade's assault [C]. A character cannot open a menu and 'learn Mana Method' without knowing it exists.
TRUE MAGIC — not 'Mana Method level 10'. With high Mana Method mastery and a compatible natural attribute, natural mana generates the REAL element (true lightning, true fire) rather than a mana construct shaped like it, and it interacts with the world by real rules [C]. Many attributes have no meaningful 'true' version.

entries.name: Ki
entries.content:
KI — perception of life-force and bodily intent, separate from mana [C]
Yami Sukehiro teaches Asta to sense ki: reading the flow of a living body to anticipate movement and attacks, even from beings without mana [C]. It is strongly associated with the Land of the Sun (Hino); advanced Hino applications exist in later canon (such as Zetten) [V].
Record in techniques with category 'Ki': sensitivity, interpretation, combat reading, emotional reading, concealment detection, prediction.
Ki gives physical and intentional information — tensing, gathering, the moment before a strike. It does not reveal health numbers, spell names, grimoire contents or future actions. Predictions can be wrong, and feints can fool it.
It is learned through a teacher who knows it, meditation, and deliberate practice under pressure.

entries.name: Ultimate Magic
entries.content:
ULTIMATE MAGIC — an elven secret technique that embodies the totality of a mage's magic in one unique spell [C]. Humans can reach it only under special conditions involving deep soul and mana understanding, Mana Method or True Magic, and natural mana [C-V].
It is unique to the individual and should be generated from the whole save: signature spells, recurring themes and imagery, relationships, combat history, major breakthroughs, attribute mastery and personal growth. A lifelong Fire mage who protects allies with lion-like close combat reaches something that feels like THAT life — never a generic 'Fire Ultimate #3'.
It requires knowledge that very few people possess; a teacher with genuine knowledge (or equivalent discovery) is almost always necessary. It is endgame-rare.

entries.name: Magic Stages, Arcane & Saint
entries.content:
MAGIC STAGES — an in-world assessment, not the engine.
Canon scale: Stage Nine (lowest) to Stage Zero (highest), originating as the Heart Kingdom's assessment of magical capability and adopted by others later [C]. ARCANE Stage marks irregular magic that defies conventional assessment and can affect devils [C]. SAINT Stage is a separate spirit-related state tied to offensive spirit magic that can purify malice and destroy devils [C].
Rules: stages are shown to the player only after legitimate assessment in an appropriate place and era (Heart first, others later). Before that, a Clover villager speaks of 'strong' and 'weak', never 'Stage Seven'. The hidden engine is more detailed than any stage; improvement does not produce 'STAGE UP!' — people are reassessed when it makes sense. Arcane is a classification flag, not a tier above Zero.
Record an assessed stage in magic_profile.stage (default 'unassessed').

entries.name: Spirits & Spirit Bonds
entries.content:
SPIRITS — independent beings, never equipment [C]
The four great elemental spirits exist exactly once each: Sylph (Wind), Salamander (Fire), Undine (Water) and the great Earth spirit [C; the Earth spirit's canon identity and host are a GAP — do not assert them]. Canon anchors: Sylph ('Bell') bonds with Yuno [C]; Undine has an ancient covenant with the Heart royal line and bonds with Queen Lolopechka [C]; Salamander is with the Eye of the Midnight Sun's Fana early in canon and later with Fuegoleon Vermillion [C-V]. Hosts are timeline-dependent; a spirit whose host dies seeks another worthy, compatible host — possibly an NPC, possibly no one.
Bond record: compatibility, trust, synchronization, mana harmony, communication, shared experience, contract status, spirit-dive potential. The spirit keeps its own personality and can disagree.
Spirit magic amplifies compatible magic and opens techniques. Spirit contract ≠ Spirit Dive (merging closely with the spirit) ≠ Saint Stage — each is its own development requiring capability and circumstance. Spirits grow alongside their hosts.
Never selectable at creation; a great spirit cannot duplicate for the player. Lesser, unnamed nature spirits may exist where canon leaves room — mark them simulation-generated.

entries.name: Devils, Hosts, Contracts & Five-Leaf
entries.content:
DEVILS — underworld beings with ranks, personalities and goals [C]
Hierarchy: low, mid, high and highest ranks; power largely decides status. Named devils are unique entities and never duplicate. Canon names include Lucifero (Gravity; king of the underworld) [C], Megicula (Curse; Vanica Zogratis's devil) [C], Liebe (bound to Asta's grimoire; the source of Anti-Magic) [C], Zagred (Word magic; orchestrated a catastrophe five centuries ago) [C-V], Beelzebub, Astaroth, Lucifugus, Lilith, Nahamah, Adramelech, Baal [names C; powers V]. Nacht Faust hosts several low-rank devils [C].
Crossing into the living world requires a valid mechanism: forbidden rituals and sacrifice, a host body, a five-leaf grimoire, or extraordinary events such as the Tree of Qliphoth [C]. No random devil encounters.
Hosts: a host gains access to the devil's attribute alongside their own. Contracts are literal bargains — access level, cost (sometimes pieces of the host's body), restrictions, influence, control, synchronization. More devil power changes more than damage: mana and output, accessible abilities, physical traits, risk and control all shift. Devil Union (host and devil fused in cooperation, as Asta and Liebe eventually achieve) requires a real relationship [C].
FIVE-LEAF: a Clover grimoire state tied to devils; a devil can make use of a five-leaf [C]. It is never generated at an ordinary ceremony, never selectable in Natural creation, and requires a valid transformation history. Devil power is never a creation option.
Generated devils may exist where canon leaves room, but must respect the hierarchy — no secret supreme devil above Lucifero.

entries.name: Negative Mana, Forbidden Magic & Curses
entries.content:
NEGATIVE MANA & FORBIDDEN MAGIC
Negative mana belongs to the underworld and Forbidden Magic [C]. It can amplify magic enormously while corrupting body, soul and magic. Track exposure, amount, source and corruption risk in conditions and world_truth. No free buffs.
Forbidden Magic is a category of methods, not a skill node: knowledge, rituals, magic stones, negative mana, sacrifice, specific artifacts or devil interaction. The UI shows 'unknown' until the character truly learns something. Using it is a crime in most jurisdictions and a moral and physical hazard.
CURSES are lasting magical effects bound to a target: they follow rules set by the curse's nature and caster, can be warded against, and are hard to lift — often requiring the caster's defeat, specialized magic or rare knowledge. Canon: the devil Megicula's curses afflict several important people across the kingdoms [C]. Curses are treated physically in the conditions list: source, effect, progression, known remedies.

entries.name: Anti-Magic
entries.content:
ANTI-MAGIC — a special power, not a magic attribute [C]
Asta, born with no mana, wields Anti-Magic through the devil Liebe bound to his five-leaf grimoire, channeling it through swords such as the Demon-Slayer Sword; it negates and disrupts magic on contact [C].
Rules: it can never be selected, randomly generated or duplicated. It still needs speed, strength, timing, Ki, sword skill, positioning and control: Asta must reach, strike or otherwise touch the magic, and scale, concentration and amount matter. Overwhelming output, distance and clever spellwork remain dangerous to its user.
Resolution: evaluate contact, amount, concentration, scale and special conditions against the magic structure. It is never an instant-win tag.

entries.name: Races, Souls & Magical Heredity
entries.content:
RACES: humans (default, including witches and Hino-born), elves (an ancient race massacred about five centuries ago, whose reincarnation drives a later canon arc) [C], dwarves (Charmy Pappitson is half-dwarf) [C-V], devils, spirits, and other beings as canon supports. Race affects lifespan, mana traits, soul properties, physical traits, hybrid inheritance, culture and compatibilities. Natural creation is human; other races only in Full Sandbox, and the world reacts honestly — an elf child in Hage would not go unnoticed.
SOULS: each major character has a soul state (integrity, reincarnation, foreign soul, devil or spirit connection, corruption, alteration). It sits dormant until reincarnation, possession or soul magic makes it matter; the body is not always the whole character.
HEREDITY: magical traits tend to follow parents without being deterministic [C]. A child may inherit one parent's attribute, a related or derived attribute, a characteristic shaped by both, or — under exceptional causes — something unusual. Mana potential follows lineage tendencies across generations with real variance; outliers stay possible. Dual attributes need a valid cause (hybrid ancestry, devil host, soul phenomena, artificial modification).
Children of the player or NPCs are generated from parents, lineage, race, household wealth, place, culture and era, then become independent people whose personalities are their own.

entries.name: Magic Tools & Artifacts
entries.content:
MAGIC TOOLS — real technology in the economy
Brooms are the most common magic tool; they let even weak mages fly [C]. Communication devices exist as carried objects [C]. Other tools cut the user's mana cost or grant functions outside their normal magic (transport, lighting, healing, storage, recording). Using one draws on the SAME output, control and mana as any other act of magic (see Magic Core Law) — a weak or poorly-controlled mage can still activate a tool, just unsteadily or wastefully; this is not a separate ability to have or lack.
Tool record: function, mana source and cost, stored mana, activation, requirements, capacity, durability, condition, creator, provenance. Tools can break, run dry, be stolen, need repair, and differ in quality and price.
Economy: makers, materials, craftsmen, regional availability, maintenance, black markets and military restrictions. A character can build a whole life as a magic-tool craftsman or engineer.
Unknown tools found in the world have function UNKNOWN until tested, identified, researched or recognized; activating an unknown artifact can be genuinely dangerous. Famous artifacts are unique and keep their provenance (creator, purpose, discovery, owners).
Inventions spread through the world if they work and are taught, changing prices, tactics and even canon events.

entries.name: Compound Magic & Team Techniques
entries.content:
COMPOUND & TEAM MAGIC
Two compatible mages can combine effects, but never as simple addition. Ask: are the spells physically and magically compatible? Are the mages coordinated? Can their control synchronize? What emergent behavior results?
Repeated cooperation builds a combination concept with participants, component spells, compatibility, coordination, shared experience and stability; it may become a practiced team technique or formal compound magic.
Squadmates who have fought together for years coordinate far better than strangers. Relationships therefore matter in battle without becoming '+10 friendship damage'.

entries.name: Magic Research, Observation & Teachers
entries.content:
MAGIC RESEARCH & LEARNING
Characters can study magic through libraries, teachers, observation, experimentation, grimoires, dungeon texts and enemy encounters: observe → record → study → experiment → understand → adapt. Knowledge (stored in codex with category 'magic') lowers the difficulty of related shaping and opens concepts.
Observation grants inspiration, not copying: a Wind mage watching rotating Water defenses may gain 'rotational defensive flow' as a concept for their own attribute.
Teachers need knowledge, teaching skill, willingness and time; they may require a relationship, payment or membership. They change training efficiency and which concepts the student meets — they cannot grant what the student's magic cannot do.
Education differs by background: nobles learn theory, history, etiquette and politics; rural upbringings teach terrain, weather, animals and survival. Neither is 'stupid'.

entries.name: Training Engine
entries.content:
TRAINING ENGINE — permanent core, before and after joining any organization.
A training job: duration (hours · days · weeks · months · custom), intensity (Light · Moderate · Hard · Extreme), primary focus, up to two secondary focuses (each added focus lowers efficiency), trainer (solo · companion · teacher · squad · custom), location, interruption mode. Write it to training_job with active true.
Focuses: mana capacity · mana control · mana output · mana sensing · physical conditioning · combat · a specific spell · spell shaping (a named concept) · a technique the character actually knows of · attribute experimentation · recovery · study · custom free training ('spend the month trying to compress wind into cutting threads').
Growth = quality × intensity × duration × potential headroom × recovery quality × teacher × environment × novelty × the character's response — then diminishing returns. A fifteen-year-old's first hard month moves a lot; the tenth identical month moves little. New challenges restore growth.
Magnitudes (0–100 hidden scale, per month of focused Hard training for a young, fresh trainee): primary focus +2 to +5, secondary +1 to +2; Moderate about 60% of that, Light about 30%, Extreme about 130% with sharply higher risk. Halve gains for each doubling of how far above the character's current level the stat already is relative to potential. Capacity only grows toward potential. Update the matching bands whenever a value crosses a band.
Fatigue and risk: every block produces physical, mana and mental fatigue, injury risk and overtraining load. Hard needs real recovery; Extreme cannot be sustained — weeks of it cause strained mana pathways, spell instability, exhaustion, injuries and forced rest that erase gains. What counts as 'Extreme' depends on the character; yesterday's extreme becomes today's moderate.
Food, lodging, money and obligations still apply during training. A job, a squad duty or family needs consume hours.
Spell concepts progress through the Spell Shaping rules; breakthroughs follow the Manifestation rules — training raises the odds of the right conditions, never guarantees a page. Technique-type focuses (mana sensing, reinforcement, Mana Skin, Mana Zone, Mana Method, Ki, or any technique the character already knows of) work the same way as spells for visibility: the hidden magic_profile number moving is not enough on its own. The first time one is meaningfully trained, push a new techniques[] entry (tier "Novice"); as it improves, update that entry's tier to match — this is what the Grimoire's Techniques tab actually reads, so a training block that doesn't touch techniques[] will look like nothing happened even though the hidden number moved.
Summaries report what actually changed in qualitative terms plus notable events ('Day 24: you held the compressed edge for eleven seconds'). A successful month can produce no new spell.

entries.name: Advance Time, Routine & Interruptions
entries.content:
ADVANCE TIME & ROUTINE
LIVE play advances minutes and hours. ROUTINE runs the character's standing schedule (routine variable: morning, day, evening, night, weekly notes and automation toggles such as auto-meals, auto-shopping, auto-rent, auto-work). ADVANCE runs an explicit skip or a training job.
Process in simulation ticks (days for short skips, weeks for long ones): training progress, recovery and fatigue, food and money, wages and bills, relationships, NPC schedules and life events, missions and squad activity, markets, world events, canon events, rumors reaching the character. Then check: does anything require the player's decision? If yes, STOP at that exact moment and hand it over. If no, continue.
Interruption modes (sim_settings.interruptions or the job's own): Cinematic — only major developments; Balanced (default) — major developments, meaningful opportunities, breakthroughs; Simulationist — smaller character events too; Do Not Interrupt — resolve everything possible except what truly needs a decision. Always stop for: being attacked or combat, serious injury, a grimoire reaction or manifestation opportunity, an important summons or offer, a crisis of someone close, a major event at the character's location, and a KNOWN scheduled event the skip would pass — ask: stop before it, or continue and miss it.
Summary format after a skip: elapsed time; work (shifts, earnings, expenses); training outcomes in bands; concept progress; relationships that shifted; prices or local news the character noticed; rumors learned; injuries or illnesses; anything left unresolved. Then play resumes at the stop point.
State at the end: world_date, world_time, elapsed_days, weather, mana/stamina/fatigue/vitality, money, inventory changes (food eaten, items used), training_job (active false when finished, or updated progress), spell_concepts, relationships, known_events, chronicle for milestones.
The world did not wait: other people trained, married, moved, got promoted, took the mission, or died. Canon events inside the window resolved if their causes held.

entries.name: Rest, Sleep, Recovery & Overtraining
entries.content:
REST & RECOVERY
Sleep: a full night restores stamina to 90–100, mana to 85–100 and removes 20–35 fatigue, less with injuries, illness, bad lodging, cold, hunger or stress. Short naps help a little. Missing sleep compounds fatigue and hurts focus, control and reaction.
Rest while awake: stamina +10–30 per hour, mana +10–15 per hour when calm.
Fatigue bands: 0–30 fresh · 31–60 tired · 61–80 worn (training gains fall, mistakes rise) · 81–100 exhausted (injury risk, spell instability, collapse possible). Overtraining load builds when Hard or Extreme blocks lack recovery; it lowers gains and raises injury and mana-pathway strain risk (add a condition).
Injuries recover over realistic time: bruises days, sprains one to three weeks, fractures six to twelve weeks, deep wounds weeks with infection risk — shortened by competent healing magic, never erased by a five-minute rest.
Recovery days still pass in the world: work may be missed and wages lost, bills continue, people visit or don't.

entries.name: Combat — Advanced Interactions
entries.content:
COMBAT — ADVANCED INTERACTIONS (loads by keyword; the live engine loads during combat)
Spell collision: compare attribute interaction, output, density, structure, control, velocity, angle and special properties → one overwhelms, both disperse, deflection, penetration, absorption, explosion, transformation or persistent interaction. A small water bolt vaporizes against a huge flame; a massive controlled wave drowns weak fire.
Magic carries physical properties where appropriate (temperature, mass, hardness, conductivity, sharpness, momentum) plus registry-defined supernatural properties. Terrain and structures have material and integrity; big spells permanently change battlefields, start fires, collapse buildings and hurt bystanders — which affects reputation, discipline, law and missions.
Barriers and Mana Skin: evaluate penetration against density, stability and reinforcement; disrupted Mana Skin takes time to re-form. Mana Zone users can strike from within controlled space; overlapping zones contest control.
Mana Method in combat: arrays take formation time and concentration; complex arrays under pressure can fail.
Flight: brooms and flight spells differ in speed, maneuverability, stability and cost; riders can be knocked off; falls from height are lethal without a method to stop them.
Anti-Magic negates on contact; its wielder must still reach the magic. Dark Magic pulls in other magic; Spatial Magic needs its own rules (range, known destination, marks) — never free teleportation.
Weapons: reach, mass, balance, damage type, handling, durability; sword skill is independent of magic power; magic can combine with weapons only when attribute, spells and skill support it.
Restraints bind what they physically bind: a bound caster may still speak, move legs, use magic not needing the bound limbs, or try to break free.

entries.name: Injury, Pain, Conditions & Healing
entries.content:
INJURY & CONDITION MODEL
conditions[] entries: {"id","kind":"injury|status|illness|curse|exhaustion","location","type","severity":"minor|moderate|serious|critical","effects","treatment","healing":"0-100%","since"}.
Injury types: cuts, punctures, burns, fractures, crushing, concussion, internal trauma, magical injuries, curse effects, amputation when circumstances genuinely cause it. Location matters: a leg wound slows movement; an arm wound impairs gestures, weapons and some casting; an eye injury limits vision; broken ribs limit breathing and endurance; a concussion hurts focus and control.
Pain and shock rise with severity; adrenaline and willpower let people keep going, but will does not repair tissue. Bleeding worsens over time without treatment.
vitality (0–100) is the hidden reserve for continuity: minor wound −3 to −8, moderate −8 to −15, serious −15 to −30, critical −30 to −50. At 0 the character is dying; death follows sim_settings.consequences (Lethal: death is possible; Grievous: the character survives mortal wounds with lasting consequences).
Status conditions (poison, paralysis, sleep, confusion, mana disruption, blindness, burning, freezing, restraint) have physical or magical causes, progression and treatment — not just icons.
Healing magic depends on the healer's attribute, spell, skill, mana, the injury's type and severity, the time since injury and any interference. Weak healing cannot fix catastrophic damage; healing never resurrects — dead is dead unless an established canon mechanism and its real prerequisites apply. Healing costs the healer mana and time; the healed may still need rest.
Update conditions as healing progresses, and remove entries (delete by index) when fully healed. Injuries affect work, training, travel and relationships.

entries.name: Team Combat, Orders, Surrender & Escape
entries.content:
TEAM COMBAT & NPC TACTICS
Every ally and enemy has an independent position, knowledge, goal, target, condition and resources. Companions are not extensions of the player's turn.
Orders ('Noelle, cover the civilians!') are requests the recipient interprets according to trust, personality, their own perception and the situation — they may adapt, improve or refuse absurd orders. Recognized leaders get more compliance.
Coordination grows with shared experience, communication, trust, familiarity and tactical understanding. Allies can intercept, shove someone clear, block, counter or take the hit through the same reaction rules.
NPC combat personalities: aggressive, cautious, defensive, tactical, protective, reckless, opportunistic, supportive — flexible under pressure (a cautious parent turns reckless to save a child).
Enemy knowledge: first sight of a spell means observation; later they remember and adapt; recurring rivals learn habits; established patterns can be broken to bait them.
Surrender depends on fear, injury, odds, personality, mission, loyalty and what they expect from you. Escape is physical — distance, line of sight, routes, hiding, valid spatial magic — and pursuers can follow. Captured people remain world entities: restrained, transported, questioned, imprisoned, rescued, escaping later.
Retreat is legitimate and never shamed by the narrator; NPCs judge it by circumstance.
The party variable tracks who is currently with the player: {"id","name","condition","mana","distance","notes"}.

entries.name: Combat Aftermath & Consequences
entries.content:
COMBAT AFTERMATH — combat persists into life
When a fight ends, nothing magically resets: injuries remain, mana stays spent, items stay used, gear stays damaged, buildings stay broken, the dead stay dead, witnesses remember, crimes may be reported, property damage has owners, relationships shift.
After any serious fight, resolve: casualties, injuries, property and environmental damage, consumed items, equipment damage, witnesses, crimes, reputation and relationship effects, discoveries, spell development, mission effects, historical significance (chronicle entry).
Growth comes from what happened, not XP: sword use → sword skill; dodging → combat experience; repeated use of a spell → its proficiency; experimentation → concept progress; exhaustion → possible adaptation after recovery; fighting beside someone → coordination; studying an opponent → knowledge.
Difficulty emerges from the world: a forest wolf may be easy, a trained knight dangerous, a captain terrifying, a supreme devil something no sane person fights because of a rumor.

entries.name: Households, Family & Social Class
entries.content:
HOUSEHOLDS & FAMILY
The civilian unit is the household: members, relationships, residence, social standing, income sources, expenses, money and savings, debt, food stores, possessions, property, dependents, reputation, obligations and history. Household funds are not the player's money: a noble's child has an allowance, not the treasury; a poor family may depend on what the player earns.
Family generation follows the chosen background with weighted realism — not everyone gets a happy nuclear family, but tragedy is never added just for drama. Family members are persistent NPCs with their own jobs, magic, moods, goals and schedules. They can need help, give help, argue, worry, fall ill, age and die.
Family magic lineage records known attributes, mana tendencies and notable ancestors, which matters for nobles, royals and for the player's future children.
SOCIAL CLASS in Clover is structural: royals and nobles hold power, wealth and institutions; commoners work; Forsaken Realm peasants face poverty and contempt. Treatment depends on the individual NPC's personality, but prejudice exists: clothing, surname, accent and residence all register. Other kingdoms have their own hierarchies (Diamond's military, Spade's regime, Heart's traditions); never paste Clover's ladder onto them.
The household variable holds {"members":[{"name","relation","age","occupation","status"}],"wealth":"destitute|poor|modest|comfortable|wealthy|noble|royal","house_name","residence","obligations":[]}.
NOBLE OR ROYAL GENERATION: the moment a household's wealth becomes "noble" or "royal" — the
player's own or any NPC's — check world_truth.houses for one that already fits before inventing
a new one. If a new house is genuinely needed, name it immediately ("House <Surname>", matching
how every canon house is named) and record it there with its tier and standing, distinct from
the four canon houses (Silva, Vermillion, Kira, Vaude — see Canon Cast) unless Sandbox explicitly
placed the character in one of those. Once named, a house is real and recurring, not a one-time
label: other nobles know of it, it has a reputation and standing among the others, it can be
gossiped about, invited to things, owed favors, or hold a grudge — treat it with the same
persistence as a named person, not simulation texture that fades once mentioned.

entries.name: Work, Jobs & Wages
entries.content:
WORK & EMPLOYMENT — BLACK CLOVER YUL ECONOMY (v21.4, deterministic payroll and treasury modules are authoritative)
Jobs are persistent positions: employer, occupation, location, agreed wage, schedule, colleagues, duties, advancement; hiring depends on skill, magic, availability, class prejudice, demonstrated reliability and current openings. No guaranteed work and no payments without a genuine contract or completed work. The engine, not GM, credits monthly Magic Knight payroll; ordinary non-knight work remains tracked via actual employer/job interactions and wages awarded exactly once.

CANON-SUPPORTED FOUNDATION [C]: Yul is Clover currency; a new Magic Knight such as Asta receives around 200,000 Yul on his first payday (Chapter 10 / Episode 11). Rank and merit/stars affect career pay and privileges. In the Volume 6 Assorted Questions Brigade, Tabata is reported to have said that even the lowest Magic Knight makes more than a regular Clover Kingdom citizen's average ANNUAL income. Treat that as a strong inequality/relative-wealth constraint, NOT as a published table of civilian incomes. Five official classes (5th → 1st) exist in Junior, Intermediate and Senior tiers, followed by Grand Magic Knight and Wizard King. The notion that all squads issue equivalent base pay for equal government rank is a deliberate simulation policy, not a canon-confirmed written pay scale.

SIMULATION, NOT CANON: Standard monthly base pay by formal rank/class (Yul): Junior 5th 200,000; 4th 215,000; 3rd 230,000; 2nd 250,000; 1st 275,000. Intermediate 5th 310,000; 4th 350,000; 3rd 395,000; 2nd 445,000; 1st 500,000. Senior 5th 575,000; 4th 660,000; 3rd 760,000; 2nd 875,000; 1st 1,000,000. Grand Magic Knight baseline 1,200,000. Wizard King's resources/compensation are exceptional state appropriations determined in-world, not a recurring ordinary rank salary. Vice-captain and captain are APPOINTMENTS, not alternate classes; office benefits and separate duty allowances may apply while appointed, but do not change formal rank pay by default.

MERIT: Confirmed individual merit stars can augment monthly pay by 1% of rank base PER PERSONAL STAR (capped at +15%) under this game's government service allowance; this exact formula is a simulation, NOT established canon. Do not confuse squad gold/black star totals with personal merit: squad stars change team standing and budgets; black stars can create investigations and disciplinary action, never arbitrary salary deduction. Captains may approve ONE-TIME specific merit/dungeon/mission bonuses only if the reward is genuinely authorized and funded; issue them as mk_payroll.bonusAwards objects with unique id, status:'approved', reason, amount, source. Do not credit money separately; the UI credits bank_account exactly once. Star awards themselves are not cash and do not automatically trigger lump-sum payouts.

PAYROLL: Recognized knight service begins when mk_status.squad and mk_status.rank are set. The engine sets the current game date as the salary anchor on first recognition to avoid retroactive windfalls in legacy saves; then it credits a secured payroll/treasury account at each following monthly anniversary, handles skipped months without duplicate credit, and preserves previous payments. Pay is not delivered as physically carried 1-Yul coins or automatically withdrawn. Transfers between squads do not restart service. Leaving/expulsion pauses pay until reinstatement; bonuses must not pay after departure. GM may narrate captain handing over a payslip when naturally encountered, but must never emit [money:+salary] or bank_account credit for an engine-paid period. Your coin balance, purchases, donations, equipment and civilian savings are NOT automatically rescaled.

CIVILIAN INCOMES — GAMEPLAY RECONSTRUCTION, NOT CANON: Peasant, day-labor and low-wage town households may see 3,000–10,000 Yul/month in cash, craftspeople and steady urban workers 8,000–16,000 Yul/month cash; unusual high-skill mages, merchants and nobility can earn much more. Subsistence farming, barter, room/board, family wages, patronage, unreliable seasons, and uneven regional prices matter. Average ordinary annual wage is NOT given numerically in canon; the simulation should preserve the sharp canon class gap without claiming these are official national statistics. A 200,000 Yul MONTHLY knight salary greatly exceeds the annual cash wages of many ordinary workers, and junior knights often support whole households. Noble Magic Knights may enjoy substantial independent family wealth but receive NO higher government base simply for bloodline.

EARNINGS VS PURCHASING POWER: Yul is modeled at roughly ¥1 of nominal purchasing power as a GAME DESIGN BASELINE only; this is not an officially confirmed exchange rate or a modern Japanese economy. Regional supply, noble monopolies, war, magic inputs, import scarcity, poverty, local food production and household barter frequently break apparent yen parity. See Economy, Prices & Trade for new price anchors. Show economic effects in family expectations, requests for support, class prejudice, taxes, dependence on powerful households and career choices. Do not automatically make peasant citizens comfortable because nominal prices are yen-inspired.

entries.name: Economy, Prices & Trade
entries.content:
ECONOMY — YUL NOMINAL SCALE, REAL LOCAL MARKETS
CANON: Clover Kingdom money is Yul (ユール); no official exchange rate with modern Japanese yen has been verified. DESIGN MODEL: 1 Yul ≈ ¥1 for nominal item-price intuition ONLY, not convertibility, inflation index, or assumption medieval Clover has Japanese salary distribution. Existing in-progress contracts and confirmed prices remain valid. Maintain persisted shops/stock rather than instant universal repricing; new stock and newly quoted prices follow the new baseline.
GAMEPLAY PRICE ANCHORS IN YUL (NOT CANON): typical retail bread 80–250 (rural self-grown or subsidized staples may be far cheaper); inexpensive meal 300–900; tavern meal 800–2,000; inn bed/night 2,000–7,000; work shirt/trousers 2,500–9,000; sturdy boots 5,000–14,000; travel pack 3,000–12,000; ordinary broom 20,000–100,000; basic sword 12,000–75,000; basic treatment 1,000–12,000; functional enchanted/magic tool 30,000–500,000+; modest rented room 12,000–55,000/month; modest town family rent 35,000–100,000/month. These are median-ish town/shop price guides, not universal floors; low-income villages survive partly via household production, informal credit, barter, pooled resources, subsidized housing and local pay-in-kind. If a price is dramatically below these bands, explain why (shortage relief, subsidy, damaged stock, barter, theft, old fixed contract) rather than silently inventing a discount.
Each market has physical stock and actual goods, buyers, sellers, transport, capital, taxes, security, seasonal supply, faction politics and region-specific wealth. Price = anchor × locally justified conditions: scarcity, supply roads, quality, craftsmanship, class targeting, heavy magic investment, kingdom borders, transport risk, counterfeits, reputation, bargaining, and recent world events. Scarcity can multiply prices; agriculture can reduce local food cash cost. Don't inflate goods solely because the player just earned a large stipend, nor suddenly grant merchants infinite budget.
Squad uniform: issued at joining, not bought at a generic clothing stall. Grimoire: never bought or sold in ordinary shops. A store transaction is applied ONCE; the UI already deducts money and moves stock into a physical container, and a following GM scene must not duplicate it. Money is the one authoritative `money` variable, and payroll is a transfer credited ONCE by the engine only after in-world due dates.
OTHER KINGDOMS: preserve their canonical systems and infer conversion/exchange/fees only where needed; the Yul nominal scale is not imposed universally.

entries.name: Housing, Property & Storage
entries.content:
HOUSING & PROPERTY
The character always has a residence state: family home, church or orphanage, noble estate, royal residence, squad quarters, rented room, inn, camp, or homelessness. Housing has an owner, occupants, rooms, storage, rent or debt, condition, security and furnishings.
Physical storage is literal: a sword left under the bed is under the bed; coins locked in a chest are in that chest; moving out without them leaves them behind. Items stored at home are NOT usable elsewhere. The property variable lists places the character owns, rents or has access to: {"id","name","type","location","status":"owned|rented|family|quarters|access","rent","storage":"...","notes"}.
Property is an asset with value, condition, occupants, income, debt and fees; it can be bought, inherited, built (construction takes materials, labor, money and time), rented out, damaged or lost.
Rent and bills come due on schedule; if auto-rent is on in routine and money allows, pay it automatically and mention it only in summaries; if money runs short, surface the problem.
HOME AND SQUAD STORAGE: When in the exact established home_location, the physical UI may store/retrieve items at that residence within a simulated 150 kg / 150 bulk room/chest allowance. When physically at their own squad HQ, current members may use the squad locker (100 kg / 100 bulk). These are mechanical storage allotments, not a claim that everyone owns a large enchanted vault; equipment is in its last actual place, subject to moving, eviction, theft and fire if causal events occur. No remote item moves. Different properties/rooms do not share contents automatically. Cash belongs in a secure bank account, not invisible unlimited pockets.

entries.name: Business, Crafting & Magic-Tool Making
entries.content:
BUSINESS & CRAFTING
Businesses have owners, locations, employees (real NPCs with pay, morale and the freedom to quit), capital, cash, inventory, suppliers, customers, income, expenses, debts, taxes or fees and reputation. They can grow, stall or fail. Owning one runs through the same economy — there is no tycoon overlay.
Supply chains are physical: ore → transport → purchase → forging → product → sale. Break a link and prices, production and jobs change.
CRAFTING: a project needs a design, materials, tools, a facility, skill and time; it can go wrong; quality follows skill, materials and care. Materials have hardness, weight, mana conductivity and capacity, durability, rarity, workability and special properties.
MAGIC-TOOL MAKING needs knowledge, suitable materials, a design, mana engineering, tools and time; results can be unstable or unique. Repair restores damaged weapons, armor, brooms, buildings and tools.
Crafting is available only with the relevant skill, tools and place. A player can make an entire life of it.

entries.name: Romance, Marriage, Children & Aging
entries.content:
ROMANCE, MARRIAGE & THE LONG LIFE
Attraction, romantic interest, emotional attachment, compatibility, comfort and trust are separate. Someone can find the player attractive and dislike them, love them and be furious with them, or respect them with no romantic interest at all. There is no romance meter to fill with gifts, and an NPC may simply not be interested.
Hard invariant: attraction is not consent; a relationship is not consent; marriage is not consent. NPC autonomy always holds. Keep intimacy off-screen or tasteful.
Courtship happens through time together, outings, gifts that fit, meeting families, talking about expectations, arguments and reconciliation, becoming exclusive, or separating. Culture, class, family and era shape courtship; noble and royal matches carry politics.
Marriage is a world event: household merger, finances, property, family and organizational reactions, inheritance. Children become full NPCs whose magic comes from the heredity rules and whose personalities are their own.
Aging: age = world date − birth date. Children grow, adults age, careers change, people retire and die of age, illness or accident — not randomly for drama. player_age increases on the character's birthday.
Legacy: if the character dies or retires, the world state supports continuing as a descendant or another person in the same world.

entries.name: Reputation, Rumor & Fame
entries.content:
REPUTATION, RUMOR & FAME
reputation is keyed by community or organization: {"Hage villagers":{"band":"...","note":"..."}, "Magic Knights":{...}}. Bands: Unknown · Noticed · Known · Respected · Admired · Renowned · Legendary, or negative: Disliked · Distrusted · Notorious · Hated. Someone can be a hero to villagers and despised by nobles.
Rumor objects (world_truth.rumors): source, claim, accuracy, importance, spread rate, regions reached, who has heard, distortion. News travels with people — travelers, merchants, soldiers, letters — with delay and change. A four-leaf in a Forsaken village becomes 'apparently two peasant kids got four-leafs' by the time it reaches the capital.
Fame has reach (Hage → the Forsaken Realm → the capital → the kingdom → abroad) and strength, both earned by deeds with witnesses.
Visibility: people cannot know about a grimoire, ability or deed they have never seen or heard of. The player can reveal, hide, lie about, allow or correct rumors; success depends on witnesses and evidence.
Only the character's legitimate knowledge appears in known_events and codex.

entries.name: Law, Crime, Witnesses & Justice
entries.content:
LAW, CRIME & JUSTICE — no wanted stars
A crime is an event with an act, place, time, perpetrator, victims, witnesses, evidence, jurisdiction and whether authorities know. Law is jurisdictional and era-specific: Clover law is not Heart law, and a future government may differ.
Detection chain: act → were there witnesses? → did they recognize the person? → will they report it, and to whom? → is the report believed? → investigation. Magic complicates evidence (illusion, transformation, spatial movement, possession, memory effects). Investigators reason from evidence, never from GM omniscience, and can accuse the wrong person.
Evidence: physical damage, stolen goods, documents, mana traces (readable only by skilled people), testimony, injuries. Chain of custody matters.
Arrest can be complied with, questioned, fled, resisted or escalated politically — each with consequences. Trials weigh accusations, evidence, witnesses, prosecution, defense and the decision-maker; in Clover, the Magic Parliament conducts formal trials of significant cases, chaired by Damnatio Kira [C]. No automatic conviction because the engine knows the truth.
Wanted status is information spread through institutions: a village that has not received the notice does not recognize anyone. Self-defense is judged by who started it, perceived threat, force used, ability to retreat where local law cares, and testimony.
Prisons are physical places where time continues: visits, transfers, escapes, releases, rescues. Status and connections influence treatment, which is itself part of Clover's injustice.

entries.name: Food, Survival & Lifestyle Automation
entries.content:
FOOD & SURVIVAL — quiet in town, vital in the wild
Hunger, hydration and nutrition are tracked quietly. In a settlement with money and access, meals happen automatically (routine auto-meals) and are mentioned only when relevant. Missing meals degrades stamina recovery, focus and training gains; extreme training needs good food to recover.
Food is physical inventory with portions and freshness; it spoils. Expeditions need supplies: rations, water, fuel, shelter. Survival detail scales with context — a city dinner is a line of prose; a three-week trek through a Grand Magic Zone makes every ration count.
Foraging, hunting and fishing depend on knowledge, skill, season, weather and what is actually present; resource nodes deplete and regrow slowly.
Camping advances world time; watches can be assigned in dangerous areas; poor sleep reduces recovery.
Lifestyle automation (routine): auto-meals, auto-basic-shopping, auto-rent, auto-work. When automation fails (no money, no food, closed shop), surface the problem instead of silently fixing it.

entries.name: Knowledge, Education & the Codex
entries.content:
KNOWLEDGE & THE CODEX
codex[] holds what the CHARACTER knows: {"topic","category":"people|places|factions|magic|history|rumors|secrets|languages","text","source"}. It grows through experience, conversation, reading, schooling, briefings and rumor, and it may contain mistakes or outdated information. Push entries when the character genuinely learns something noteworthy; keep text short. When it grows past about 60 entries, merge older minor ones.
Two modes: CHARACTER KNOWLEDGE (immersive; only the codex) and LORE REFERENCE (out of character: the player may ask the GM for canon lore; answer respecting spoiler_level, and do not add it to the codex).
Literacy and education follow background: noble upbringings bring history, politics, magic theory, etiquette and languages; rural lives bring farming, terrain, weather, animals and local dangers. Libraries, tutors, military instruction, the Magic Knights, apprenticeships and self-study all teach. Not every settlement offers the same education.
known_locations[] holds geography the character knows: {"name","kingdom","region","status":"visited|known|rumored","notes","route"}. Maps and guides can add or even mislead.

entries.name: Local Events & Emergent Problems
entries.content:
LOCAL EVENTS — stories without canon
Settlements generate events from their state: failed harvests, delayed caravans, missing children, mine accidents, beast attacks, business disputes, thefts, weddings, festivals, fires, new shops, appointments, feuds, magical accidents, strange discoveries.
Causal chains create opportunities: heavy rain → damaged bridge → interrupted trade → flour delayed → bread prices rise → the baker cannot stock up → she asks someone she trusts for help. If that someone is the player, it is a personal opportunity; if not, someone else may solve it.
Recurring calendar: grimoire ceremonies (March), the Magic Knights Entrance Exam (annual), markets, festivals, harvests, tax periods, military rotations, religious observances, trade cycles. Canon events sit on top of a world that already has a calendar.
Push only what the character learns into known_events; opportunities expire or get taken by others ('Position filled').

entries.name: Clover Class Prejudice, Clothing & Social Etiquette
entries.content:
CLOVER CLASS, DRESS AND PREJUDICE — AUTHORITATIVE SOCIAL SIMULATION
Authority: Black Clover canon establishes powerful royal houses, lesser nobility, commoners and marginalized peasants; the detailed etiquette bands and thresholds here are explicitly SIMULATION INFERENCES, not numerical manga canon. This rule extends Visible Equipment, Clothing & Social Perception, Households & Family, Reputation/Rumor, the canon-character profiles, and NPC Knowledge. Apply the rules to characters of ALL origins, not solely the player.

ACTUAL STATUS VS WHAT IS PERCEIVED
- Real origin comes from player_profile.social_origin / household and established NPC/house records. Birth, house membership, money, income, institutional rank, surname, recognized insignia, magic proficiency, and social reputation are DISTINCT. Wealth does not grant noble birth; a borrowed royal cloak does not establish royal identity. Nobles may also be impoverished, badly dressed or disliked.
- appearance_state.social is computed locally from physically WORN items and the current location; it is not an NPC's knowledge. It distinguishes visible fabric quality, wear/cleanliness, formal style, recognized-looking uniform, armor, visible weapons, and venue. Use it as physical evidence only. The UI never automatically broadcasts it to bystanders.
- A stranger may infer class from tailoring, accent, etiquette, surname, companions, residence, documents, family symbols and widely known deeds, but may be wrong. Knowledge of someone's TRUE background requires plausible recognition, introduction, records, gossip already received, a revelation, or prior acquaintance. No mind-reading through HUD fields. Mark incorrect assumptions as the NPC's own belief, not narrative fact.
- Apparent wealth, heroic gear and Magic Knight status can create contradictory signals. Prejudice need not disappear when the evidence contradicts stereotypes; characters may rationalize it as luck, patronage, theft, insolence or an exception. Conversely, respectful people can recognize merit regardless of birth.

BLACK CLOVER HIERARCHY — ASYMMETRIC, NOT UNIVERSAL HOSTILITY
- ROYALTY (e.g., Kira, Silva, Vermillion) have hereditary prestige and access, but personalities differ. Some are explicitly snobbish; some value skill, duty and kindness. Being a royal does not make every individual abusive.
- NOBILITY often enforce class boundaries, titles, invitation protocols, patronage and appearance standards; some are benevolent, practical or quietly sympathetic. They may distinguish an ordinary commoner merchant from a remote Forsaken Realm peasant, and they may look down on fellow nobles with no standing or poor presentation.
- COMMONERS have trades, neighborhoods, distinct levels of wealth and education. A respected urban merchant might be impeccably dressed while a poor laborer wears work clothes. They may admire or resent nobility, have biases against peasants, or treat outsiders as equals.
- PEASANTS/FORSAKEN REALM RESIDENTS face heavier structural disrespect and fewer opportunities in elite Clover institutions. Their poverty is a recurring economic reality, not an intrinsic personality, cleanliness, inferiority, intelligence, magical incapacity, or a permanent wardrobe. A peasant in good clothes is still a peasant if their origin is known.
- MAGIC KNIGHTS and exceptional achievements can complicate the ranking, not erase it. Rank matters IF known and authentic, and uniforms/insignia matter IF actually worn or legitimately recognized. A hostile noble may grudgingly obey a common-born captain while still insulting their birth. Squad customs vary (Black Bulls, Golden Dawn, etc.). Authority cannot be claimed merely by clicking on a uniform.

APPEARANCE, CONTEXT, CONSEQUENCES — CHECK THESE EVERY RELEVANT SOCIAL SCENE
1. WHO OBSERVES? Only NPCs already present, positioned to perceive, awake and attentive. Identify their own standing, established temperament, agenda, ties to the player and what they realistically know; a bystander may be silent or distracted.
2. WHERE? Compare ordinary markets, village work, taverns, military barracks, squad headquarters, noble estates, upper-class shops, palace/court audiences, formal ceremonies and private rooms. The Royal Capital is a WHOLE CITY, not permanently a throne room. Compare the local kingdom; Clover's four-class ladder should not be blindly applied to Heart, Diamond or Spade.
3. WHAT IS ACTUALLY VISIBLE? Check appearance_state.coverage, clothing, appearance_state.social (fabric quality, condition, ceremony fit), visibleArmor, drawnWeapons and notableGear. A sheathed sword worn by an actual Magic Knight may be normal; a drawn weapon at court is another matter. Dirty boots after a mission are not proof someone was born a peasant.
4. EXPECTATION VS PRESENTATION: A simple clean tunic is fully appropriate in a market; in a royal gala it can mark a guest as underdressed. A luxurious gown at a village fair may impress or be inconvenient; a peasant dressed extravagantly at court may be mistaken for a servant in costume, a sponsored attendant, a wealthy commoner, or a noble depending on existing evidence. A noble in muddy field gear can attract censure too. Damaged, bloodstained, ill-fitting, conspicuously revealing or otherwise inappropriate clothing matters in formal contexts when observed.
5. POWER AND HISTORY: A named royal/landowner can ignore, humiliate, overcharge, rebuff, order a servant to intervene, deny a private audience, impose rules or quietly show kindness, but only within actual institutional authority and plausible actions. Public mockery can provoke bystander discomfort, gossip, allies defending the player, an invitation lost, or a guard requiring credentials. Not every slight is an arrest, and an NPC cannot retroactively change a completed equipment action.
6. RESPONSE FREQUENCY: Class pressure is persistent even without spoken insults. Favor expressive, varied behavior over obligatory comments: a cold look, moving the queue, pointed titles, an usher stepping between guests, a shopkeeper switching tone, a whisper, a deliberately ignored greeting, a reluctant salute, occasional explicit classist dialogue. NPCs react when the social moment or contrast makes it pertinent, not once per turn and not to every garment. Dignity, politeness and expertise vary by person. Do not flatten all royal/noble NPCs into the same voice.

INTERACTION EXAMPLES (ILLUSTRATIVE, NOT GUARANTEED EVENTS)
- A PEASANT arriving at a noble reception in patched traveling clothes: the usher may question the invitation, keep them waiting or ask them to use a service entrance. If the same person is a decorated knight in a visibly authentic uniform, the usher may have to admit them while a prejudiced guest sneers about their birth.
- A COMMONER merchant wearing exquisite tailored clothes: a courtier may compliment the cut before demanding family credentials; a less prejudiced noble may assess the quality of their merchandise. Fine clothes don't counterfeit a pedigree.
- A NOBLE wearing torn, dirty clothes at court: rival nobles may whisper, suspect disgrace or criticize respectability despite knowing their lineage. A ROYAL in informal clothes may face propriety and family scrutiny while retaining rank.
- A PEASANT wearing a rare enchanted weapon in a public square: interested nobles might ask its provenance, regard it as suspicious, attempt to recruit the wielder, envy it, or ignore it if they have other concerns. Uncommon equipment is not automatically proof of a crime.
- An UNDRESSED character in a crowded court hall: public-decency and access concerns become much more pressing than tailoring, handled nonsexually and with age-appropriate boundaries. In a private changing room the same physical condition is unremarkable.
- For canon NPCs, prioritize established individual characterization: Solid/Nebra may be ostentatiously contemptuous, while Mimosa or Fuegoleon may be more considerate. Nozel's reactions depend on his obligations and character development, not a generic 'all royals sneer' template.

COST AND AUTHORITY BOUNDARY
- The player pressing Equip/Remove/Store/Drop/Use ordinary items directly updates inventory, carry_state, appearance_state and equipment_activity. NO model call, chat message, forced NPC line, reputation penalty or free NPC event is produced by that click. The UI can show a deterministic equipment description and social-presentation cues at no mushies cost.
- On the NEXT real GM scene with an actual perceiving NPC, consult CURRENT appearance_state and known social identities, NOT merely the last equipment event. If the character changed clothes twice between scenes, others only see the present outfit unless they actually witnessed a change.
- No fabricated witnesses, spontaneous offscreen publicity or class-specific punishment from an unwitnessed UI click. Changes to relationships/reputation/rumors/property/access must be justified by concrete events already resolved and recorded. Only explicit 'Use in story (AI)', dialogue, combat or other normally narrated actions invoke AI when needed.
- Distinguish a CHARACTER'S biased judgment from the narrator's objective truth. Render discrimination plausibly without endorsing it. Classism matters to decisions, access, wages, trade, marriage politics and institutions, but never removes player agency.

entries.name: Clover Kingdom ♣
entries.content:
CLOVER KINGDOM ♣ ([C] confident canon · [V] verify-level · [S] simulation-derived)
Government: King Augustus Kira Clover XIII of House Kira, vain and image-obsessed [C]. The Wizard King, Julius Novachrono (Time Magic; cheerful, magic-obsessed), leads the Magic Knights and is the kingdom's greatest mage and symbol [C]. The Magic Parliament holds formal trials, chaired by Damnatio Kira [C]. The three royal houses are Kira, Silva and Vermillion [C]; noble houses include Vaude, Roselei, Unsworth, Boismortier and many generated houses [C/S].
Social order in concentric realms [C]: the Noble Realm at the center (Royal Capital, castle, estates), the Common Realm around it (towns, cities, merchants, artisans), and the Forsaken Realm at the edges (poor villages near dangerous borders). Class prejudice is daily reality; higher classes tend to have more mana — a tendency, never a law.
Magic in daily life: brooms, magic-assisted chores and crafts, enchanted tools. Strong magic brings status; a talented Forsaken-born mage meets suspicion.
Canon places: Royal Capital — Clover Castle, Castle Town, Magic Knights headquarters, squad bases (the Black Bulls' hideout is an odd building that moves thanks to Henry's magic) [C] · Hage — Forsaken Realm village with the church-orphanage of Father Orsi and Sister Lily and a grimoire tower [C] · Sosshi ('Saussy') — Forsaken Realm village attacked by the Eye of the Midnight Sun early in canon [C] · Kiten — Common Realm city near the Diamond border, site of a major Diamond attack [C-V] · Nairn — Common Realm town [V] · Raque — seaside town; the Seabed Temple lies beneath the nearby sea [C] · Ultime-Volcano region — volcanic land of violent mana used for brutal training [V]. Unlisted villages and roads are simulation-filled and permanent once generated.
Borders [C]: Diamond (hostile; recurring border fighting), Heart (mostly peaceful, distant), Spade (distant; a later-era threat); the Witches' Forest is a neutral land between Clover and Diamond; Grand Magic Zones lie in the neutral lands.
Currency: yul [C]. Life paths: farming, trade, crafts, church, local guard, noble service, independent mage work, research, crime — or the Magic Knights via the annual Entrance Exam.
Opening-era politics: squads compete for stars and prestige; Golden Dawn leads, the Black Bulls are mocked; nobles dominate institutions; the terrorist Eye of the Midnight Sun is emerging; Diamond presses the border.
Clover origins (page III): Royal — House Kira, Silva, Vermillion or a cadet branch (real expectations, scrutiny, marriage politics); Noble — a generated or custom house; Commoner — urban, merchant, artisan, military or rural household; Peasant — village, farming, church or orphan upbringing, laboring household. The character is never an unknown member of a canon family's inner circle unless Sandbox says so.

entries.name: Diamond Kingdom ♦
entries.content:
DIAMOND KINGDOM ♦
A harsh, militarized land of mines and wasteland whose poor resources drive expansionist war, especially against Clover [C]. Its soldiers are Mage Warriors; the strongest are the Eight Shining Generals [C]. Mage Scholars, led by Moris Libardirt, perform human experiments — implanted mage stones, grimoire and body modification — to manufacture stronger mages; Mars (Mineral Magic) is one such product [C]. Lotus Whomalt (Smoke Magic) is a Diamond mage met in early canon [V]. Other generals' names are not verified here — generate unnamed figures rather than inventing 'canon' names.
Canon gives no Clover-style class ladder; use simulation backgrounds [S]: influential household, military household, scholar household, merchant or mining household, ordinary citizen, poor laboring household, orphan or state ward.
Life: rationing, conscription pressure, propaganda, informants, the prestige of battlefield service, research-district secrecy. Regional state to track in world_truth.diamond: ore production, food supply, military demand, border pressure, morale, research funding, conscription pressure. A new mine can change a region; a failed campaign tightens food.
