Career: civilian → recruitment → Mage Warrior training → deployment → advancement → elite service → possibly general. Enhancement offers are real, invasive, risky decisions that can alter magic, body, mind and lifespan — never '+30 magic [ACCEPT]'.
Places: the capital and military, mining and border regions are simulation-filled [S]; label them clearly as such on creation.
Default history: Diamond fights Clover at the border and in the dungeon race in the opening era [C]; later, Spade overruns Diamond [C].

entries.name: Heart Kingdom ♥
entries.content:
HEART KINGDOM ♥
A land rich in greenery, water and powerful natural mana [C]. Queen Lolopechka (Water Magic; earnest and clumsy) rules, and her line holds an ancient covenant with Undine, the great Water spirit [C]. The Spirit Guardians are the kingdom's strongest protectors (Gadjah is one) [C-V]. Heart developed Mana Method from its abundant natural mana [C], and the Magic Stage assessment originates here [C]. Through Undine and country-scale mana awareness the ruler can sense and influence the land (world_truth.heart_network) [C-V].
Backgrounds [S]: royal household (highly restricted), guardian-affiliated, mage household, agricultural, artisan, ordinary citizen, remote community.
Growing up in Heart builds familiarity with natural mana and sensing — never automatic Mana Method, which needs real instruction and a compatible attribute.
Careers: local magical work, regional protector, formal study, royal service, military or protective service, and — as a lifetime achievement, never a starting class — Spirit Guardian.
Places: the royal palace region and forest, river and lake settlements [S unless canon-named]; label generated places clearly.
Default history: Heart is threatened by Spade's Vanica Zogratis and her devil's curse [C]; before Spade's assault, Clover knights come to Heart to learn Mana Method [C].

entries.name: Spade Kingdom ♠
entries.content:
SPADE KINGDOM ♠ — the most era-dependent start
The royal House Grinberryall was overthrown by the Zogratis siblings, the Dark Triad — Dante (Body Magic), Zenon (Bone Magic) and Vanica (Blood Magic, host of the devil Megicula) [C]. They wield devil power through devil contracts [C]; Zenon's devil is Beelzebub and Dante's Lucifugus [V]. Under them Spade becomes oppressive and expansionist: it conquers Diamond and attacks Heart and Clover [C]. The Mage Defense Force, once the people's protectors, becomes the regime's instrument [C-V]. Spoilers (gate by spoiler_level): Yuno is the lost Grinberryall prince; an eldest Zogratis sibling, Lucius (Soul Magic), is the true power behind the Triad.
Backgrounds [S]: former royal loyalist, military, government-affiliated, ordinary citizen, rural, occupied or controlled community, resistance-connected, displaced or orphaned. A Grinberryall relation exists only in Sandbox or suitable alternate starts and carries enormous lore weight (the line's unusual celestial magic).
Life under the Triad: informants, purges, conscription, devil-empowered officers, fear. Serving, deserting, secretly aiding civilians, resisting, staying out of it or profiting are all the player's choices, each with consequences. The simulation never decides morality.
Devil power is never a creation option; it arises only from real circumstances.
Earlier eras: before the coup, Spade under the Grinberryalls is a very different kingdom — reconstruct it from era selection, with details simulation-filled.

entries.name: Other Origins — Witches' Forest, Hino, Neutral Lands
entries.content:
OTHER ORIGINS
WITCHES' FOREST — a neutral land between Clover and Diamond ruled by the Witch Queen (Blood Magic) [C]. Witches are powerful mages; outsiders are unwelcome and the Queen is ruthless with anyone who defies her [C]. Vanessa Enoteca fled it [C]. A witch origin means a closed, hierarchical community with unique magic and strict rule.
LAND OF THE SUN (HINO) — Yami Sukehiro's homeland across the sea [C]. Its magic uses scrolls rather than grimoires, with strong traditions of Ki and swordsmanship [C-V]. Hino-born characters never attend a grimoire ceremony; their progression runs through scrolls, teachers and Ki. Details are sparse — simulation-fill carefully and mark it.
NEUTRAL LANDS — lawless borderlands, smugglers, wanderers, small independent settlements and Grand Magic Zones between the kingdoms [C for zones; settlements S].
ELVES — an ancient race massacred about five centuries ago [C]; elf reincarnation drives a later arc. Never a Natural creation option.
Custom origins are allowed in text; validate them against the lore and generate honest consequences.

entries.name: World Geography & Map Authority
entries.content:
WORLD GEOGRAPHY — one continuous coordinate space
Clover borders Diamond, Heart and Spade, with neutral territory and Grand Magic Zones between nations [C]. Every place belongs somewhere; no scene exists just because the narrator needs one.
Location status: CANON EXACT · CANON APPROXIMATE · CANON RELATIVE · SIMULATION FILLED · GENERATED · CUSTOM. Never invent precise canon geography — choose coordinates and distances that satisfy known relations, mark them simulation-derived, and keep them permanently once used (store key distances in world_truth.geo).
The player sees relative descriptions ('three hours along the eastern road', 'sixteen kilometres from the border'), never coordinates.
Map knowledge is the character's own (known_locations): visited · known · rumored · approximate · unknown. A person who has never been to Diamond knows its famous places and little else. Maps, guides, briefings, merchants and rumors add knowledge — and can be wrong or outdated (a collapsed bridge still drawn, an old border).
World-map authority: narration may never relocate a character for convenience. If the player is in Heart when something happens in Clover, they remain in Heart. No 'somehow you arrive just in time'. COORDINATE SYSTEM: Royal Capital is the origin (0,0), km east(+)/west(-) as x, km north(+)/south(-)
as y (see the Geography Gazetteer for confirmed values, sourced from the official guidebook map).
Straight-line distance is sqrt((x2-x1)²+(y2-y1)²); a real route is always longer once roads,
terrain and borders bend around it — never just the straight-line number. player_x/player_y track
where the character actually is right now; the interface updates them on arrival for an
uninterrupted trip (see UI:TRAVEL), so you only need to set them yourself when a trip was
interrupted and ended somewhere other than the planned destination, or when a generated place
needs its first coordinate. NEW PERMANENT PLACES: assign a coordinate consistent with where the
narration has already put it, relative to the nearest confirmed place, then keep that coordinate
forever — never silently relocate something once it has a coordinate, even across a long gap in
play. GENERATED PLACES — exist first, discovered later. Before inventing any village, hamlet, farm,
ruin, shrine, crossing or camp, check world_truth.geo for one that already fits; discovery
REVEALS what already existed and never regenerates it somewhere new. When a new one is genuinely
needed: (1) decide WHY it's there first — a ford, crossroads, farmland, mine, coast, pass,
shrine, border post — then name it; (2) place it where the narration has already put it,
relative to the nearest confirmed place, with plausible spacing (villages usually 5-15 km apart
along roads, never two permanent places on the same spot); (3) respect Clover's concentric realms
[C], which follow distance from the capital: Noble Realm within about 10 km, Common Realm about
10-38 km, Forsaken Realm beyond about 38 km out to the borders [S, derived from the confirmed
coordinates] — a 'Forsaken village' 15 km from the capital is a contradiction, not a detail;
(4) keep other-kingdom places inside that kingdom's region; (5) record it in world_truth.geo
immediately, with its kind, realm and reason. Named interior spots you describe inside it (its
inn, well, smithy, chapel) go in that record's places list and stay put on every later visit.
A place the character has only heard of may enter known_locations as status approximate with a
rough position; on actually arriving, refine it by a few km at most, never relocate it.

entries.name: Travel Engine
entries.content:
TRAVEL — time, cost and risk are real
Travel time = distance × terrain × road quality × weather × transport × traveler condition × load × party pace × interruptions. Nothing is a fixed number; once a route's distance is established it stays consistent.
Modes and rough speed by terrain, km/day on a full travel day (roads/plains · forest or rough
country · mountains) [S, anchored to the qualitative canon pace already established]: on foot
25-35 · 15-20 · 10-15. Horse 45-65 · 25-35 · 15-20. Carriage/wagon 40-60 · 20-30 · 10-15 (roads
only, can't take rough country). Ship (coastal/river routes only) 60-100. Broom 30-60 km/h in
active bursts, not a day-rate — needs rest, mana, navigation and safe landings, so treat it as
several fast hops rather than one continuous flight.
Special modes, each gated by real requirements, never a free fast-travel unlock: Spatial Magic
(a Spatial mage opens a door between two places; both ends need to be somewhere the mage has
genuinely been or can otherwise anchor to — near-instant, but entirely dependent on having that
specific mage along) [C]. Star Magic (a Star mage can only return to a star they themselves
already placed — instant, but requires prior setup, not spontaneous long-range travel) [C]. A
Recombination-linked structure (like the Black Bulls' own base) can relocate itself, but that
moves the building, not the character freely — it's not a mode the player chooses on demand [C].
Travel groups move at the pace of the slowest or most injured member; members can disagree about routes.
Default flow: BEGIN TRAVEL → simulate the route → stop only for meaningful events (a decision, danger, discovery, blocked road, important encounter, severe weather, a border, injury, a major world event, a relevant opportunity) → ARRIVE. Scenery is summarized, never 'you keep walking' turn after turn.
Encounters are state-based: who is actually on this road? Merchants, farmers, patrols, animals, bandits, knights, scouts, travelers — or, often, nothing unusual. People met on the road keep moving after you part.
Update current_location on arrival (or wherever the leg actually ends, if interrupted), spend food and money, and add new places to known_locations — the interface now owns stamina, mana, fatigue, world_time and world_date for travel (see the UI:TRAVEL protocol); report the real elapsed hours via last_travel_report instead of writing those directives yourself.

entries.name: Borders, Citizenship & Cross-Kingdom Travel
entries.content:
BORDERS & CITIZENSHIP
Borders have checkpoints, fortifications, legal and illegal crossings, security level, diplomatic state, trade policy, military activity, smuggling and current restrictions. Diplomatic state (peace · tense · skirmishes · hostile · war · occupation) changes scrutiny, trade, routes, patrols, prices and civilian movement.
Characters carry citizenship, residency, travel documents, military or faction credentials. A Clover Magic Knight wandering into Diamond during conflict is in grave danger; a civilian merchant faces different questions.
Illegal crossing (wilderness, smugglers, disguise, flight, spatial magic, forged papers) is possible and genuinely risky. No 'border locked until quest 12'.
Reputation is per country: respected in Clover, unknown in Heart, wanted in Spade. Nothing locks the player into their starting kingdom.

entries.name: Weather, Climate & Mana Geography
entries.content:
WEATHER & MANA GEOGRAPHY
Each region has climate (temperature range, rainfall, seasons, winds, elevation) and daily weather (temperature, precipitation, cloud, wind, visibility, storms). Weather changes travel, flight, fire, water, survival, roads and combat. Keep the weather variable current as a short phrase.
A second, invisible map tracks natural mana: density, flow, turbulence, stability and attribute biases [S]. Canon establishes that mana is uneven and that very dense areas produce abnormal environments [C]. Mana-rich places affect spellcasting, magical wildlife, rare materials and settlement.
GRAND MAGIC ZONES (Strong Magic Regions) — areas of exceptionally dense, dangerous mana, many in the neutral lands [C]. Their danger is environmental — heat, turbulence, distortion, wildlife, visibility — not a level requirement; the right technique can matter more than raw power. Canon examples: the Ultime-Volcano (intense heat and uncontrolled mana; Mana Skin is vital) [V], the Seabed Temple area near Raque [C], the Gravito Rock Zone of floating rocks [V]. Temporary mana storms and anomalies may be generated; mark them simulation-generated.
Training in such places can develop Mana Skin, sensing, natural-mana awareness and Mana Zone — only if the character actually survives and trains there. Exposure does not raise raw potential.

entries.name: Wilderness, Camping, Ecology & Tracking
entries.content:
WILDERNESS & ECOLOGY
Between settlements lie wilderness cells with biome, terrain, mana, vegetation, wildlife, resources, trails, ruins, camps, landmarks and threats. They stay lightweight until entered and change gradually with geography — farmland does not reroll into lava desert.
Creatures live as populations with habitats, prey, predators, breeding and migration; magical creatures depend on mana and environment. No monster spawns behind you because the story wants a fight; generated creatures respect region, ecology and power limits (no ancient dragon outside Hage).
Landmarks and discoveries persist; a cave the player names 'Wolf Cave' keeps that name if it spreads.
Tracks and evidence: footprints, wheel ruts, campfires, blood, broken branches, burned ground, mana residue. Reading them needs skill; tracking needs information, not a glowing arrow.
Camps: shelter, fire, food, water, watches, visibility and security; poor rest reduces recovery.

entries.name: Exploration, Discovery & Knowledge Markets
entries.content:
EXPLORATION & DISCOVERY
EXPLORE uses a time budget, movement, a search method and character knowledge. Intensity: casual · thorough · exhaustive — more time, more fatigue, more exposure to hazards, a better chance to find what is really there. Searching never creates new places.
Hidden locations have visibility (vegetation, terrain, illusions, secret entrances); people can walk past them repeatedly. NPC explorers may find things first and keep them secret, sell the location, claim it, loot it or tell friends.
Information has value: maps to dungeons, rare-herb locations, safe routes through Grand Magic Zones, smuggling paths, mana-rich training spots — sold, stolen, shared, outdated or false. Rumored locations appear as rumors with a source and unknown reliability.
Exploration is a full career: explorer, cartographer, treasure hunter, researcher, dungeon specialist, guide, merchant-explorer. Maps are information objects with accuracy, detail, errors and dates.

entries.name: Dungeons
entries.content:
DUNGEONS — world events and locations, never farmable instances
Black Clover dungeons are dangerous ancient structures full of magical traps and valuable treasure, which can appear unexpectedly; kingdoms race to claim them because their artifacts matter strategically [C]. Dense mana distorts their interiors: spaces larger than the outside, shifting gravity, walls that become floors [C].
Emergence: a hidden structure becomes exposed through mana changes, erosion, earth movement or world events; discovery then spreads through reports and rumors, and expeditions race in. The player is rarely guaranteed to be first.
Generation happens once and is fixed: floors, rooms, connections, traps, hazards, creatures (native, mana-adapted, constructs, later intruders), treasures, a central treasury, structural integrity and collapse conditions. Fog of war: the player knows only what they have explored or mapped. No corridor appears because a fight is needed.
Traps are physical state — attribute, trigger, effect, detection difficulty, disarm methods, charges, reset behavior. A spent single-use trap stays spent; a destroyed mechanism stays destroyed.
Treasure never respawns. Taken items leave the dungeon; if Diamond gets there first, Diamond has it. Removing a primary treasure can collapse some dungeons [C]; others collapse differently or not at all.
Ownership after exploration: discovering and controlling factions, contested claims, border incidents. On official missions, finds usually belong to the kingdom or squad; personal claims, theft and smuggling create consequences.
Unknown artifacts have unknown functions until identified; some are dangerous to activate. Ancient writing needs scholarship, translation or special ability. Mana Skin is harder to maintain amid dungeon turbulence.
Canon default: early in the Magic Knights era a new dungeon appears near the Clover–Diamond border, drawing Black Bulls, Golden Dawn and Diamond forces (Mars, Lotus) [C-V].

entries.name: Magic Knights — Institution, Ranks, Stars & Career
entries.content:
MAGIC KNIGHTS OF CLOVER — CANONICAL INSTITUTION & GAMEPLAY PAYROLL
Clover's nine squads serve the Wizard King. Joining is optional; missions and promotions follow achievements, not levels or XP.
CANON [C]: Every recruit starts at Junior Magic Knight FIFTH CLASS regardless of noble/commoner/peasant origin (including royals). Promotion order: Junior Fifth→Fourth→Third→Second→First; Intermediate Fifth→Fourth→Third→Second→First; Senior Fifth→Fourth→Third→Second→First; Grand Magic Knight; then Wizard King (exceptional appointment). Vice-captain/captain are service offices; not rank substitutions. Promotions are institutional, normally involving formal merit recognition and the awards system; never advance the rank silently from a star counter.
CANON [C]: Magic Knights receive regular pay; salary/privileges increase with standing. Asta's first payment was about 200,000 Yul; Yuki Tabata's Volume 6 Q&A is reported to say even the lowest knight's earnings exceed an ordinary citizen's average ANNUAL income. Game's specific rank pay table and first-payday timing are reconstructions, not published canon.
GAME POLICY: equal BASE rank pay across squads; high-status squadrons may have better quarters/squad gear and discretionary bonuses but NOT larger state base pay for nobles or Golden Dawn. Separately tracked personal family wealth is NOT government pay. Individual stars (mk_status.personal_stars) provide +1% rank-base monthly service allowance/star up to +15% [SIMULATION, not canonical formula]; squad gold and black stars affect organization prestige, funding, career reputation and disciplinary risks, without automatic cash conversion. Genuine authorized one-time dungeon/combat/protection bonus can be approved with a stable ID in mk_payroll.bonusAwards, which the UI credits to bank_account once.
PAYROLL AUTHORITY: All routine Magic Knight salary and approved bonuses are engine/UI-owned via the mk_payroll ledger, based on real in-game calendar dates, never per message. GM updates mk_status.rank/squad/personal_stars on real promotion/merit and may approve performance bonuses; it never writes routine [money] salary or directly mutates bank_account, rewrites cyclesPaid, or claims unpaid wages already arrived. Squad captain is the narrative distributor, not an independent source of duplicate money. Unpaid periods while unassigned are not funded. Grand/Wizard King exceptional rules are in Work & Wages.
Squad life: headquarters duties, training, comrades, command structures, star competition, conflicts, travel and class discrimination persist. NPC witnesses need plausible knowledge of a member's squad and official rank to react to visible wealth, expensive uniforms, or privilege; a wealthy-looking peasant Magic Knight does not become a noble.
mk_status records squad, rank, merit, personal_stars, since, captain and exam; affiliations[] records institutional connections; mk_payroll records authoritative paid service, approved awards, and money transfers.

entries.name: The Nine Squads — Opening-Era Snapshot
entries.content:
THE NINE SQUADS — Opening-Era snapshot ([C] confident · [V] verify · update rosters by era)
• BLACK BULLS — Captain Yami Sukehiro (Dark Magic; from the Land of the Sun; Ki; gruff, lazy-seeming, fiercely loyal: 'surpass your limits') [C]. Rowdy misfits who opened the series at -30 stars [C], their headquarters a rundown, patched-together house that moves thanks to Henry Legolant's Recombination Magic [C]; funding and shared equipment are threadbare to match, even as individual members grow formidable. Members: Magna Swing (Fire; peasant-born, loud, proud senior) [C]; Luck Voltia (Lightning; smiling battle maniac) [C]; Vanessa Enoteca (Thread; a witch who fled the Witches' Forest; drinks) [C]; Finral Roulacase (Spatial; disinherited elder son of House Vaude; flirt) [C]; Gauche Adlai (Mirror; obsessed with his sister Marie) [C]; Grey (Transformation; painfully shy) [C]; Gordon Agrippa (quiet, eerie, lonely; poison- and curse-type magic [V]) [C]; Charmy Pappitson (Cotton Magic; food-obsessed; half-dwarf [V]) [C]. Asta and Noelle Silva (Water; a royal with poor control early) join after the exam [C]; Zora Ideale (Ash; traps) and Secre Swallowtail (Sealing) join later [C]; Nacht Faust (Shadow; devil host) is the unseen vice-captain [C, spoiler].
• GOLDEN DAWN — Captain William Vangeance (World Tree Magic; masked; gentle; carries a secret) [C]. The elite squad, first in stars. Klaus Lunettes (Steel; stiff, principled) [C]; Langris Vaude (Spatial; Finral's arrogant younger brother) [C]; after the exam Yuno (Wind; four-leaf) and Mimosa Vermillion (Plant; healing applications; Noelle's cousin) [C].
• SILVER EAGLES — Captain Nozel Silva (Mercury; royal; cold, proud) [C]; Solid Silva (Water) and Nebra Silva, Noelle's siblings who scorn her [C].
• CRIMSON LION KINGS — Captain Fuegoleon Vermillion (Fire; royal; honorable and demanding) [C]; his brother Leopold 'Leo' (Fire; hot-blooded) [C]; their elder sister Mereoleona (Fire; ferocious; natural-mana master) later leads as acting captain [C].
• BLUE ROSE KNIGHTS — Captain Charlotte Roselei (Briar; cursed in childhood; secretly loves Yami) [C]; Sol Marron (Earth; her devoted 'big sis') [C-V].
• GREEN MANTIS — Captain Jack the Ripper (Slash Magic; lives to cut strong opponents) [C].
• AQUA DEER — Captain Rill Boismortier (Picture Magic; a very young, artistic genius) [C].
• CORAL PEACOCKS — Captain Dorothy Unsworth (Dream Magic; almost always asleep; terrifying inside her dream) [C].
• PURPLE ORCAS — Captain Gueldre Poizot [C] — details sparse here: do not elaborate his magic or loyalties; later leadership changes are spoiler-gated.
Support: Owen, the Magic Knights' healer [C]; Marx Francois, aide to the Wizard King, communication-related magic [V].

entries.name: Factions & Organizations
entries.content:
FACTIONS & ORGANIZATIONS act without the player
Kingdoms keep high-level state (ruler, government, treasury, food security, trade, military strength, stability, morale, diplomacy, wars and treaties, known and secret threats). Below them: squads, noble houses, military organizations, churches, merchant networks, criminal groups, research institutions, witch and elf communities, player-founded groups.
Each has members, leadership, resources, territory, goals, relationships, knowledge, operations and reputation. They pursue goals offscreen: recruit, feud, trade, conspire, expand, collapse.
Membership brings obligations, protection, access, politics and enemies. Loyalty, desertion, corruption and betrayal are real. The player can found an organization; it needs members, money, purpose and a reason for anyone to follow.
Canon organizations of the opening era: the nine Magic Knight squads, the Magic Parliament, the royal houses, the Eye of the Midnight Sun (terrorists), Diamond's military and Mage Scholars, Heart's Spirit Guardians, Spade's regime and Mage Defense Force, the Witches' Forest.

entries.name: The Road to the Magic Knights (Opening Era)
entries.content:
THE ROAD TO THE MAGIC KNIGHTS — a canon current, not rails
Default beats for Clover fifteen-year-olds: the March ceremony → about six months of life and training → travel to the Royal Capital → the Magic Knights Entrance Exam → captains raise their hands → accept an offer, or fail → life opens completely. None of it is mandatory.
Surface it naturally, as far as canon_guidance allows: early, 'The exam is about five months away'; later, NPC questions ('You're really taking it?'), notices, travelers heading to the capital, provisions for sale, other applicants training; eventually a known_events entry 'Magic Knights Entrance Exam — Royal Capital — N days'. The journey is real: days on foot, less by broom or carriage; it costs money and food and can be interrupted.
If a skip would pass a known exam date, stop and ask: stop before it, or continue and miss it.
The exam is annual. Missing or failing means next year's exam (different applicants, squad needs and captains' moods) — never a broken save.
Canon default (if intact): Asta and Yuno train, then leave Hage for the capital together. It is their own event; the player travels with them only if their relationship and plans make it natural.

entries.name: Magic Knights Entrance Exam — Live Simulation
entries.content:
MAGIC KNIGHTS ENTRANCE EXAM — annual, at a colosseum in the Royal Capital [C]. A huge crowd of
applicants from every realm, open to any mage regardless of social status [C]; all nine captains
attend and personally observe the whole exam, since selecting recruits is their own decision, not
a passed-down list [C].
Attending is entirely the player's choice — nothing requires pursuing the Magic Knight path at
all. But once the player has actually committed to sitting THIS exam (travelled to the Royal
Capital, on the day, at the colosseum), run it as a real staged event, in order, not summarized
straight to a result — UNLESS the player explicitly chooses to back out partway through, at which
point they simply didn't sit this year's exam; nothing is held against them and they're free to
attempt a future year's.
STAGE 1 — REGISTRATION: candidates register on arrival [C]; noble candidates openly ridicule
other examinees, commoners and Forsaken applicants especially, while this happens [C].
STAGE 2 — THE WAIT: while everyone waits for the exam to actually begin, Anti-birds — real
canon creatures drawn to weak magic — flock the venue and peck specifically at LOW magic-power
candidates, a visible, public, humiliating marker before a single test has even started; a
candidate with real magical presence draws none of this attention at all [C]. Play this
proportionally to the character's actual output/control, same as any other magic-sensitive
reaction — don't skip it as flavor, it's a real beat that happens to everyone before the tests.
STAGE 3 — THE TESTS (below).
STAGE 4 — SELECTION: captains decide individually, in front of everyone, right after watching
(see Selection below).
STAGE 5 — AFTERMATH: whatever happens next — celebration, disappointment, an offer to weigh,
a captain's first words to a new recruit — follows immediately; results are known same-day, not
announced later.
Tests (canon set; order can vary by year): broom flight; demonstrations of magical power; hitting moving targets; a creation-magic demonstration; making a seed grow (fine control); and finally one-on-one combat bouts with applicant-chosen partners.
Resolve each test from the character's actual profile, spells, techniques, equipment and condition. A poor controller wobbles on the broom; an ill-suited attribute must improvise; six months of focused shaping can surprise everyone. Record notable moments. These tests read out capability the character already has — magic_profile output and control, sensing, and any spells or techniques already on hand — through freeform demonstration; they are not a spell-concept factory. Broom flight in particular is a pure baseline check (functioning mana plus basic output and direction into an object), not a spell at all, which is exactly why a mage with no ordinary mana reserve cannot do it regardless of whatever other power they have. A genuinely novel freeform attempt during a test CAN seed a new spell_concepts entry at IDEA or EXPERIMENTAL — but it does not manifest a page on the spot; that still needs the real development the Manifestation rules describe, same as any other concept.
Captains judge independently from what they WITNESSED plus their values (simulation readings of canon personalities; log in world_truth.exam): Yami — guts, strange potential, surpassing limits; class and polish mean nothing. Vangeance — talent and future potential. Nozel — nobility, pride, elegance. Fuegoleon — strength with integrity and growth. Charlotte — capable, disciplined women; disdains brashness. Jack — ferocity and edge. Rill — creativity and the unusual. Dorothy — whimsical, often asleep. Gueldre — self-interest. Rumors (a four-leaf, noble birth) color expectations; performance decides.
Selection: each applicant steps forward; interested captains raise a hand. None → fail (next year, or another life). One → that squad's offer (accept or refuse). Several → the applicant chooses.
Canon default (if intact): every captain raises a hand for Yuno, who chooses the Golden Dawn; only Yami raises his for Asta — after Asta's bout with the noble Sekke Bronzazza — and Asta joins the Black Bulls; Noelle Silva also joins the Black Bulls [C]. The player's presence never erases canon applicants' competence.
State: mk_status.exam {year, status, notes, offers}, then mk_status squad and rank ('Junior Magic Knight, 5th Class') and affiliations, chronicle, relationships with the captain and squadmates, reputation among the Magic Knights.

entries.name: Canon Characters — Runtime Rules
entries.content:
CANON CHARACTERS ARE PEOPLE (runtime rules)
Each canon character carries identity, age by era, personality, values, goals, fears, habits, magic, grimoire, spells, techniques, occupation, rank, squad, home, current location, schedule, relationships, knowledge, memories, injuries and alive-state. Keep per-save facts in world_truth.npcs.<id> and player-facing ones in relationships.
Snapshots, not a timeless sheet: load the version that fits the start date. A younger Yuno lacks later spells and knowledge; an older Asta has lived his history. Every important ability has an acquisition point — before it, the character cannot use it unless divergence created a valid earlier path, and then their grimoire answers the life they are actually living rather than unlocking the exact canon spell early.
Decisions come from personality + goals + relationships + knowledge + obligations + location + resources + perceived risk + emotion + recent events. If the world still matches canon's prerequisites, the canonical choice is highly plausible; otherwise simulate. Ask 'what would this person do now, knowing what they know?', never 'what did chapter 73 say?'.
Canon NPCs do not know their future, their arc, or that they are canon. They remember the player: a friend of ten years is never treated as a stranger because a canon scene only included Asta.
Everyone uses the same progression engine as the player: mana, training, grimoire growth, injuries, teachers, experience, relationships, environment.
States: alive · dead · missing · captured · incapacitated · sealed · unknown. Dead is dead unless an established mechanism with its real prerequisites applies. NPCs know only what evidence gives them; a missing person is not 'dead' to others just because the engine knows.
Presence never steals: canon characters keep their competence when the player is present, and the player keeps their accomplishments.
Canon anchors below are tagged [C] confident or [V] verify-level. Never elaborate a [V] detail beyond what is written; prefer the player's correction for [V] items. Unknown numbers stay unknown in canon — derive simulation values and mark them in world_truth.

entries.name: Canon Cast — Hage, Asta & Yuno
entries.content:
CANON CAST — HAGE (Forsaken Realm, Clover)
ASTA [C] — orphan left at Hage's church as a baby alongside Yuno; born with no mana at all in a world where everyone has some; loud, blunt, relentlessly determined, trains his body obsessively; dream: become Wizard King. Pre-ceremony: no grimoire, no Anti-Magic — both arrive only through the ceremony-night events. Protective of the church kids; proposes to Sister Lily constantly and is always refused.
YUNO [C] — orphan raised with Asta; quiet, composed, fiercely competitive; enormous innate mana and natural control; Wind Magic; also dreams of becoming Wizard King; outwardly aloof, loyal underneath. Receives a four-leaf grimoire at the ceremony and later forms a bond with the wind spirit Sylph ('Bell') [C]. Hidden origins are heavy spoilers (see Spade).
FATHER ORSI [C] — the priest who runs Hage's church and orphanage; dramatic, kind, poor. SISTER LILY [C] — a young nun who raised the orphans; warm, strict, perpetually rejecting Asta's proposals. The church children — Recca, Nash, Hollo, Aruru and others [V names] — live there too.
REVCHI SALIK [C] — a former Magic Knight turned thief who comes to Hage on ceremony night to steal Yuno's four-leaf; his attack is when Asta's five-leaf appears. Details of his magic are unverified here.
Hage itself: a poor farming village near the kingdom's edge with a grimoire tower; people are hardworking, gossipy and not rich [C]. Generate other villagers (farmers, the tower master, merchants) as persistent NPCs.
If the player grows up in Hage, Asta and Yuno are real neighbors of their own age: they can be friends, rivals, strangers or nuisances depending on what the player does.

entries.name: Canon Cast — Crown, Parliament & Royal Houses
entries.content:
CANON CAST — CROWN, PARLIAMENT & ROYAL HOUSES OF CLOVER
Julius Novachrono [C] — Wizard King; Time Magic; affable, endlessly curious about all magic, fond of disguises and wandering; pragmatic about politics; formidable. Heavy later spoilers exist about him — gate by spoiler_level.
Augustus Kira Clover XIII [C] — the King; vain, jealous of the Wizard King's popularity, weak as a ruler.
Damnatio Kira [C] — chairman of the Magic Parliament; severe, cold, obsessed with 'justice' in his own image.
House Silva [C] — royal; stern, proud, military. Nozel (eldest, Silver Eagles captain), Solid and Nebra (arrogant siblings), Noelle (youngest, water magic she cannot control at first, looked down on by her siblings); their late mother Acier was a legendary knight [C].
House Vermillion [C] — royal; fiery, strong-willed. Fuegoleon (Crimson Lions captain), Leopold (his brother), Mereoleona (their wild elder sister), Mimosa and Kirsch (cousins; Mimosa is Golden Dawn) [C].
House Kira [C] — the reigning royal house.
House Vaude [C] — noble house of spatial mages: Finral (disinherited, Black Bulls) and Langris (heir, Golden Dawn).
Owen [C] — senior healer serving the Magic Knights. Marx Francois [V] — the Wizard King's aide.
A player of royal or noble origin belongs to a GENERATED branch or house unless Sandbox explicitly places them in a canon family; canon families never gain members who did not exist in canon.

entries.name: Canon Cast — Eye of the Midnight Sun & Early Threats
entries.content:
CANON CAST — EYE OF THE MIDNIGHT SUN (opening-era terrorist group)
A group seeking revenge against the Clover Kingdom, led by a masked man called Licht who wields Light Magic [C]. The true identities and history behind him are heavy spoilers (elves, five centuries ago) — gate by spoiler_level.
The Third Eye, its elite trio [C]: Rhya (copy-type magic) [V], Fana (Flame Magic; host of the fire spirit Salamander) [C-V], Vetto (Beast Magic; brutal) [C].
Other members met early [C]: Heath Grice (Ice Magic; leads the attack on Sosshi village), Valtos (Spatial Magic; Licht's aide), plus others such as Rades Spirito and Sally [V].
Their operations follow the default history below (Sosshi village, the Royal Capital assault, the Seabed Temple, the Witches' Forest). They have spies and goals of their own; if the player's actions weaken or expose them, they adapt.

entries.name: Default History — Opening & First Magic Knights Year
entries.content:
DEFAULT HISTORY TRAJECTORY — Opening era (CY 0 = the year Asta and Yuno turn 15). Each beat happens ONLY if its causes still hold; record status in canon_state.events (DORMANT → APPROACHING → ACTIVE → RESOLVED → HISTORY, or ALTERED / PREVENTED). Dates are approximate [S] unless noted.
1 · March CY 0 — Hage Grimoire Acceptance Ceremony: Yuno receives a four-leaf; Asta none. That night Revchi Salik attacks; Asta's five-leaf appears (Anti-Magic) [C].
2 · Following months — Asta and Yuno train, then travel to the Royal Capital [C].
3 · About six months later — Magic Knights Entrance Exam: Yuno → Golden Dawn; Asta and Noelle → Black Bulls [C].
4 · Soon after — First Black Bulls mission: Asta, Noelle and Magna defend Sosshi village from Heath Grice of the Eye of the Midnight Sun [C].
5 · Early months — a dungeon emerges near the Clover–Diamond border; Black Bulls and Golden Dawn teams (including Asta, Noelle, Yuno, Klaus and Mimosa) race Diamond's Mars and Lotus inside [C-V].
6 · Soon after — the Eye of the Midnight Sun assaults the Royal Capital; Fuegoleon Vermillion is gravely wounded (loses his right arm and falls into a coma) [C].
7 · Later — the Black Bulls at the seaside town of Raque and the Seabed Temple, battling Vetto of the Third Eye; Asta's arms are ruined in the fight [C-V].
8 · Later — Asta seeks a cure in the Witches' Forest; the Eye of the Midnight Sun and Diamond both strike there; the Witch Queen's ambitions surface [C].
9 · End of the first year — the Star Awards; then the Royal Knights Selection Exam forms an elite team to attack the Eye of the Midnight Sun's hideout [C].
Outside Clover in the same window: Diamond wars on its borders; Heart stays largely peaceful; Spade is already under the Dark Triad [C-V].
The player may be present, adjacent or absent. Absent and uninvolved → resolve the beat historically at low detail and let consequences propagate (news, prices, fear, recruitment). Involved → simulate fully. Changed causes → recompute and mark divergence.

entries.name: Default History — Later Eras (spoiler-gated)
entries.content:
DEFAULT HISTORY — LATER ERAS (gate every detail by sim_settings.spoiler_level; never volunteer these in narration or OOC)
10 · Elf reincarnation: the souls of elves massacred five centuries ago possess people across Clover; the truth behind Licht, the Golden Dawn captain and the devil Zagred's manipulation comes out; the kingdom is devastated and its leadership shaken [C].
11 · Aftermath: Clover knights learn of Spade's threat; many train in the Heart Kingdom in Mana Method before Spade's assault [C].
12 · Spade's invasions: the Dark Triad strike Heart and Clover; Vanica and her devil Megicula clash with Noelle and others; Megicula's curses tie several fates together [C].
13 · The Spade Kingdom raid: Clover and Heart forces strike into Spade; the Tree of Qliphoth and the king of devils, Lucifero, come into play; the Dark Triad fall [C-V].
14 · Final arc: an elder Zogratis, Lucius (Soul Magic), pursues his own plan with 'Paladins'; Asta spends time in the Land of the Sun; the outcome of the final arc is a GAP in this build — do not assert how it ends. If a save reaches that period untouched, simulate plausibly from the state of the world and label it SIMULATED in canon_state.
Later-era starts load the world after these beats (who is alive, where, in what role, which places were damaged, who knows what). When unsure of a late-canon fact, choose the least specific consistent version and mark it simulated rather than inventing precise canon.

entries.name: Era Starts, Historical Initialization & Generations
entries.content:
ERA STARTS & THE LONG TIMELINE
The world date and the character's age are independent. Eras on creation: Before the Main Story (years before CY 0) · Opening Era (CY 0 March) · Magic Knights Era (after the exam; Asta and Yuno already in their squads) · Later Era (spoiler-safe labels until the player allows detail) · After Canon / Far Future · Custom (e.g. '3 years before', 'same year as Asta', '2 years after Asta joined').
Initialization for later starts: apply every default-history beat before the start date (or the save's divergent history), then age everyone, move people to their current roles and places, apply damage and rebuilding, update rulers, captains and squad rosters, political and international state, public vs secret history. The player enters the actual later world, not Episode 1 with a new date.
Earlier starts leave the future unresolved; canon characters are younger and lack later abilities. The player's years of life before CY 0 can change prerequisites, and canon adapts causally.
After published canon: time beyond the story is SIMULATED FUTURE, never canon. Characters age, retire, marry, have children, die; new knights and new threats appear; history becomes memory that NPCs recall according to age, place, education and involvement. The player's deeds become history the same way — decades later, people may remember 'the flame knight' with distortions.
Generational play: children inherit family, status, lineage and circumstances and develop their own personalities. If the character dies or retires, continuing as a descendant in the same world is supported.

entries.name: Canon Cast — Foreign Figures
entries.content:
CANON CAST — BEYOND CLOVER
Diamond [C unless marked]: Mars (Mineral Magic; one of the Eight Shining Generals; product of Moris's experiments; cold, conflicted); Moris Libardirt (Mage Scholar; human experimenter); Lotus Whomalt (Smoke Magic; lazy veteran) [V].
Heart [C]: Queen Lolopechka (Water; Undine's partner; clumsy, earnest; under a devil's curse in canon [V details]); Gadjah (Spirit Guardian; teaches Clover knights) [C-V].
Spade [C]: the Dark Triad — Dante Zogratis (Body Magic; cruel philosopher of 'evil'), Zenon Zogratis (Bone Magic; cold, relentless), Vanica Zogratis (Blood Magic; childlike, bloodthirsty; host of Megicula). Their eldest brother Lucius is a heavy spoiler.
Witches' Forest [C]: the Witch Queen (Blood Magic; ruthless ruler, with plans of her own).
Land of the Sun [C]: Yami's homeland; its people and clans are sparsely documented here — keep details simulation-filled and modest.
Named canon figures appear where the era and place put them; the player meets them only through plausible circumstances.

entries.name: Missions — World Problems First
entries.content:
MISSIONS — every mission starts as a world problem
Problem → a report or request → an institution decides who handles it → assignment (squad, contract, private job, favor). Nothing exists just to be a quest.
Sources: squad assignments, Wizard King orders, local officials, nobles, merchants, villages, private commissions, criminals, rumors and the character's own initiative.
missions[] entries: {"id","title","issuer","type":"mission|contract|job|favor|personal","known_objective","status":"offered|accepted|active|completed|failed|abandoned","location","deadline","reward","notes"}. Store only what the character knows. The TRUE situation (the hidden threat behind the 'bandits') goes in world_truth.
Missions have real availability: squadmates may be busy, injured or away; a mission taken by someone else is gone; deadlines pass. Rewards come from the issuer's actual resources; Magic Knight rewards mostly mean stars, merit, standing and pay rather than piles of coin.
Outcomes are not binary: partial success, collateral damage, political fallout, saved or lost lives, prisoners, reports that shape promotions.
Canon events become missions only when the character's organization would plausibly assign them; the UI never shows 'CANON EVENT AVAILABLE'.

entries.name: Relationships, Memory & NPC Initiative
entries.content:
RELATIONSHIP ENGINE
relationships is keyed by NPC id: {"npc-...":{"name","role","familiarity","trust","respect","affection","attraction","rivalry","fear","resentment","loyalty","summary","last_seen","status":"alive|missing|dead|unknown|captured"}}. ID RULE (see also Ids in the Directive Protocol): canon characters key on their own plain name — "asta", "yuno", "noelle" — never "npc-asta"; the "npc-" prefix is reserved for original characters who need disambiguation. Before adding ANYONE, check every existing key's "name" field (case-insensitive, prefix-insensitive) for a match and reuse that key if found — never create a second entry for a person who already has one. If a duplicate is ever found (e.g. during a sync pass or a player report), merge the better-populated object into the canonical key and delete the duplicate key that same turn: [relationships.npc-asta: delete].
Give a named NPC who matters a "birth_date" too, same "D Month, CY N" format as the player's own
— for a canon character, use their real databook birthday if you actually know it [C]; otherwise
treat it as simulation-derived [S] like any other unconfirmed personal detail, and once set, never
change it. An NPC's stated age should agree with birth_date and world_date the same way the
player's does — don't let a birthday quietly pass without the age around it moving too. A noble or royal NPC carries a "house_name" too, resolved the same way the player's own is — check world_truth.houses first, generate and record a new one there only if genuinely needed. Values 0–100 (fear/resentment/rivalry start at 0) describe how THAT PERSON feels toward the player; the player's own feelings are theirs to play. The UI shows only the summary line ('Trusts you deeply', 'Recent tension', 'Hasn't spoken to you in three weeks') unless numbers are enabled.
Changes follow events: shared danger, reliability, help, honesty, betrayal, humiliation, gifts that fit (gifts matter, but friendship is not bought). Typical magnitudes: small kindness +1–3; real help +3–8; saving someone +10–20; betrayal −15–40. Cap about 10 per turn except extreme events. Refresh summary when the relationship meaningfully shifts.
NPCs remember events and significant statements ('You promised you'd come back'; 'You said you hated nobles') and interpret them their own way; minor chatter fades. Promises, debts and favors go in commitments: {"kind":"promise|debt|favor|obligation","who","content","due","status"}. Breaking one hurts according to how much that person cared.
NPCs have relationships with each other, and they take initiative: visit, invite, write, ask for help, offer work, warn, lie, confess, argue, apologize, introduce someone, drift apart or move away — driven by personality, circumstances, schedule and goals.
Secrets spread only through the social network; telling one person does not tell their friends.
Rivalry need not be hostility: friendly magical rivals, professional rivals, romantic rivals and bitter enemies are all different.

entries.name: Shops & Gear Catalog
entries.content:
SHOPS — what a settlement actually has, by size
Village: a general store (food, tools, rope, candles, cloth), a smith (mundane tools, horseshoes, simple blades, repairs), maybe a single multi-purpose trader. Town: adds a tailor or outfitter, a proper armorer/weaponsmith, a magic-tool shop or peddler, an apothecary-equivalent (herbs, salves, basic remedies — medicine still exists alongside magic; healing magic is skilled and not universally available or free), a stable or broom-dealer, an inn. Capital or major city: adds specialty magic-tool engineers, a jeweler or curio dealer, importers of foreign goods, guild or squad-affiliated suppliers, and a black market for anyone with the right contacts.
GRIMOIRES ARE NEVER SOLD — they choose their owner and are not shop inventory under any circumstance; don't generate a "grimoire shop." Grimoire towers are civic/religious sites, not businesses.
GEAR — what actually gets bought (extends the price anchors in Economy, Prices & Trade)
Weapons: mundane swords, daggers, spears, staves and the like, priced by material and craftsmanship (see updated sword 12,000–75,000 Yul anchor); enchanted or masterwork weapons cost far more and are rare, named, provenanced items, not shelf stock. Most Magic Knights fight with magic first and a sidearm or none at all — Asta's reliance on swords is unusual, not standard [C].
Protection: Clover doesn't run on heavy plate — protection is mostly magic (Mana Skin, barriers, reinforcement). What's actually sold: reinforced traveling coats and gloves, simple leather or metal bracers and guards for non-mages, and squad uniforms, which are issued on joining, not purchased. Don't generate market-stall plate armor or shield walls; it doesn't fit the setting.
Travel and field gear: packs, bedrolls, waterskins, rope, tents, rations, boots and cloaks, a compass or map, a broom for those who can afford and ride one.
Magic tools (see Magic Tools): brooms, communication devices, mana-cost-reducing or function-granting tools, priced 30,000–500,000+ Yul by rarity and function.
Medicine: herbal remedies and basic first aid are ordinary commerce; potent healing is a skilled mage's service (see Injury, Pain, Conditions & Healing), not a potion bought off a shelf.
Everyday goods: cloth, tools, candles, cookware, books and paper, toys, instruments — ordinary material culture exists; invent it freely within a settlement's established wealth and character rather than treating the world as weapons-and-magic-tools only.
Any sold container uses explicit physical storage compartments. Stock may specify storage_profile as belt_pouch, travel_satchel, field_pack, magic_tool_case or quiver, plus unit weight/bulk. If the customer cannot carry a purchase, the sale is refused without deducting yul.
